INTRODUCTION 
  
  I, the Chairman of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Industry, having been authorized by the Co mmittee, hereby present this Three Hundred 
and Tenth Report on the Action Taken by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises on the recommendations /observations of the Committee on Industry 
contained in the Committee’s 304th Report on Demands for Grants (2021-22).  
  
2. The 304th Report of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee 
on Industry was presented to the Rajya Sabha on 17 th March, 2021 and laid on the 
Table of the Lok Sabha on 17th March, 2021. 
 
3. The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises furnished the Action 
Taken Notes on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s 304th Report, of 
the Committee on Industry on 3rd September, 2021. 
  
4. The Committee in its meeting held on 21st December, 202 1 considered and 
adopted the Report.

REPORT 
 
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the 
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on the recommendations  contained in the 
Committee’s 304th Report on the Demands for Grants (2021-22) pertaining to M/o MSME. 
 
2.  Action Taken Note have  been received from the Ministry of Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises  in respect of the recommendations /observations contained in the          
304th Report. These have been categorized as follows: 
 
Chapter-I-       The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry 
  Para:  28, 37, 53, 61, 73, 74, 83, 85, 86, 87, 88 and 103 (Total: 12) 
 
Chapter-II-  The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to   
pursue further in view of the Ministry’s replies. 
Para: 11, 12, 15, 17, 25, 31, 41, 43, 56, 62, 69, 70, 90 and 104 (Total: 14) 
 
Chapter-III-  The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee has not 
accepted replies of the Ministry.  
  Para: 3, 4, 13, 23, 24, 38, 39, 42, 48, 49, 54, 63, 65, 78, 79 and 84  
(Total: 16) 
 
Chapter-IV- Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the 
Ministry are still awaited.  
Para: 55  (Total: 01) 
 
3. The details of the Action Taken Replies of the Ministry and further recommendations/ 
observations of the Committee thereon wherever found necessary are given in the succeeding pages. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
 
Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
1. The Committee appreciates the effort made by the Ministry in respect of 
creating e -market linkages for strengthening the MSME Sector and recommends 
that the Ministry should analyze the marketing system of MSMEs of developed 
countries and their system of ne wer technology adoption for their development 
and adopt the best practices followed internationally for advancement and 
development of indigenous MSMEs.  
 
(Para 28) 
 
Action Taken 
 
The Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme provides market support 
to MSMEs by promoting new market access initiatives like 
organising/participation in Trade Fairs/Exhibitions, Vendor Development 
Programmes etc. with in the country. The International Cooperation (IC) Scheme 
provides financial supp ort to the MSME sector for participating in international 
exhibitions/fairs to exhibit their products.  The recommendation of Committee has 
been noted for further necessary action. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
2. PMEGP is one of the flagship Schemes of the  Ministry of MSME which is 
capable of generating large -scale employment for youth of the country, 
particularly during the Covid Pandemic. The Committee , however, finds that an 
amount Rs. 2000 crore has been allocated for the Scheme for FY 2021-2022 vis-à-
vis allocation of Rs. 2500 crores during 2020 -2021. The Committee recommends 
that more allocations should be demanded by the Ministry at the RE stage for 
effective implementation of the Scheme. 
(Para 37) 
Action Taken 
 
An amount of Rs.1905.80 crores (Margin Money of Rs.1877.33 crores+ 
Backward & Forward Linkages of Rs.28.47 crores) was allocated under the 
PMEGP Scheme for the year 2020 -21 at Revised Estimates (RE) stage. In 
addition, an unspent balance of Rs. 499.28 crore as on 1 st April, 2020 was also 
available. During the FY 2020 -21, PMEGP has performed very well and achieved 
its annual targets by assisting 74,415 applicants in setting up new microenterprises 

 
 
3 
 
through disbursing a subsidy of Rs. 2,188 crores and generating employment 
opportunities for an estimated 5.7 lakh persons.   
 
Banks during 2020 -21 have sanctioned about one lakh applications, which 
are 50% more over the last year. Approval rate of the applications forwarded to 
the banks also increased from 21.6% in 2019 -20 to 25.6% in 2020 -21. This has 
been PMEGP’s best performance since its inception in 2008 -09 despite COVID 
challenges throughout the year.  
 
For the FY 2021 -22 (Budget Estimate) an amount of Rs. 2000.00 crores 
(MM of Rs.1900 crores + B&F 100.00 crores) have been allocated. However, a 
target for setting up of at least one lakh new units under PMEGP for the year 
2021-22 has been fixed. The additional budget requirement will accordingly be 
requested in due course through Supplementary Grants.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
3. The Committee notes that the BE for SFURTI Scheme for FY 2020 -21 i.e. 
Rs. 464.85 crore was reduced at the RE Stage to Rs. 300 crore and the Actual 
Expenditure was only Rs. 192.54 crores till 31 st January, 2021. The Committee 
also notes that against a projected Budget Estimate of Rs. 500 crores for the 
SFRUTI Scheme for FY 2021-2022, an allocation of only Rs. 170 crores has been 
made. The Committee expresses its concern over the low utilization pat tern and 
reduction in allocations for an important Scheme of the Ministry, which is capable 
of generating employment in a large scale in the rural areas for the artisans, 
particularly during the Covid Pandemic. The Committee recommends that a 
holistic evaluation study of the Scheme may be conducted and based on the said 
study more allocations should be projected by the Ministry at the RE Stage for 
effective implementation of SFURTI Scheme for benefit of the traditional artisans. 
 
(Para 53) 
 
Action Taken 
 
The RE for the year 2020 -21 was Rs. 350 crores out of which Rs.349.110 
cores was utilized which is 99.74% of the RE. For FY 2021 -2022, more funds 
shall be sought at RE stage based on the progress to implement the Scheme.  An 
evaluation study of the Scheme has been under taken by IIM Lucknow.  Based on 
the report and internal assessment, the Scheme shall be carried forward with 
required changes for the benefit of the traditional artisans across the country.  

 
 
4 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
4. The Committee observes that one of the most important objectives of the 
implementation of various Schemes under Coir Board is the creation of 
employment especially in rural areas of the country. For this purpose, Coir Board 
is providing training on various  aspects of production and development of 
new/innovative products. The Committee recommends that Ministry should make 
these training courses popular through various social publicity mediums available 
so that large number of people especially from younger g eneration may get 
attracted to such training courses, which will culminate in fruitful employment. 
 
(Para 61) 
 
Action Taken 
 
Presently, the Coir Board through its Regional /Sub Regional Offices is 
making efforts to  popularize its training courses through the concerned District 
Industries Centers, Directorate of Industries, Coir Project Offices,  SHGs, NGOs, 
various co -operative societies etc. Further, through the conduct of promotional 
programs viz. Entrepreneurship Development Programme, Awareness 
Programme, Workshops, seminars etc., more people including the younger 
generation are being made aware about coir training courses.  On the website of 
the Board, videos and e-tutorials on various coir processing and applications have 
been uploaded. During the year 2020 -21, 29 National/ Regional level webinars on 
various topics on coir and Schemes and services were conducted which were 
attended virtually by more th an 35,000 participants/ viewers including from other 
social media like WhatsApp groups, Face book, You Tube etc. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
5. During the lockdown periods the availability of raw material was disrupted 
which affected the operations of MSMEs adversely. Further, the prices of raw 
material have risen exorbitantly in the recent times which have significantly 
affected the businesses of  the MSMEs and their profits have significantly 
decreased. In this given scenario, NSIC can play a significant role by 
coordinating with the respective Ministries to ensure unhindered supply of raw 
material to MSMEs and also provided support and interventi ons to the MSMEs in 
the export of their products. The Committee expresses its satisfaction that NSIC 
performed well since II Quarter and facilitated the MSMEs to the tune of Rs. 
1234.91 crores. The Committee is however, of the view that the Ministry should  

 
 
5 
 
also explore other possibilities for raw material supply to MSMEs instead of 
solely depending on NSIC to meet the raw material requirements of MSMEs . 
 
 
(Para 73) 
 
6. The Committee recommends that a robust procurement system should be 
evolved which could ensure unhindered and timely supply of raw materials to 
MSMEs at reasonable price. The Committee recommends that required steps 
should be taken to keep the prices of ra w material reasonable, including giving 
some sort of subsidy, so that MSMEs can run their businesses smoothly.  
 
(Para 74) 
 
Action Taken (For Para 73 and 74) 
 
To ensure regular supply of raw material to MSMEs, National Small 
Industries Corporation (NSIC), a CPSE under this Ministry , facilitates MSMEs in 
meeting their raw material requirements. For this purpose, NSIC enters into 
arrangements with bulk manufacturers for supply of raw materials to MSMEs. 
NSIC also provides financial assistance to MSMEs under i ts Raw Material 
Assistance Scheme against bank guarantee for payment to suppliers. 
 
Further, Government of India has taken various steps to ensure continuous 
supply of raw materials to MSMEs. Some of the steps taken to meet the raw 
material demands of MSMEs in the Steel Sector are as under:  
 Guidelines have been issued on 24.06.2020 by Ministry of Steel for 
providing limited quantum of four product categories of steel (hot rolled 
coil, cold rolled coil, wire rods and alloy steel bars) to MSME members of 
Engineering Export Promotion Council (EEPC) at export parity price by 
domestic producers.  
 Relief has also been provided to metal recyclers by exempting Basic 
Customs Duty (BCD) on steel scrap and reducing BCD to 2.5% on copper 
scrap as well as revocation/temporary revocation of ADD and CVD on 
certain steel products.  
 Besides, production of iron  ore and steel by mining companies and major 
steel producers has been increased to ensure steady availability of steel for 
use by MSMEs. 
 
 

 
 
6 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
7. The Committee observes that NSIC through its Vendor Development 
Programmes sensitize and facilitate MSEs, including SC/ST enterprises, to 
become qualified vendors to public sector enterprises and other Government 
Departments as per the provision of 25% mandatory procurement under Public 
Procurement Policy. Of this, 4% should be from SC/ST MSEs. However, during 
its visit to Kolkata, Hyderabad and Mumbai in January, 2020, the Committee 
found that while the PSUs and Government procurement from MSEs has been 
gradually improving, procurement from SC/ST units is negligible. Therefore, the 
Committee recommends that there should be more Vendor Development 
Programmes organized to popularize Public Procurement Policy among MSEs 
especially SC/ST and Women entrepreneurs. 
(Para 83) 
 
Action Taken 
 
Under National SC -ST Hub, Special Vendor Development Progr ams 
(SVDPs) are organized through NSSH Offices in coordination with 
CPSEs/Central Ministries and local industry associations to encourage the SC/ST 
enterprises to be part of public procurement. Post such outreach activities, training 
in e-tendering and handholding support for participation in Govt. Tenders are also 
provided to interested SC -ST entrepreneurs through the National SC -ST Hub 
offices located at various places. Since its inception, 335SVDPs have been 
organized under the NSSH. In addition, more th an 1500SVDPs have been 
conducted in collaboration with CPSEs and various Industry Associations.  
 
Since the inception of the NSSH, there has been a 10-fold growth in the public 
procurement from SC/ST MSEs. The procurement made from SC/ST MSEs from 
FY 2015-16 to FY 2020-21 are as under:

Recommendation/Observation 
 
8. The Committee observes that under National SC/ST Hub, the Actual 
Expenditure has always been less than the BE. The Committee is concerned about 
the under-utilization of allocated funds meant for the marginalized communities of 
the society. The Committee recommends that Ministry should endeavor to improve 
the situation by ensuring that the budget earmarked for SC/ST Hub Scheme is 
utilized fully for the benefit of the communities. Creating awareness among SC/ST 
entrepreneurs, ground level support and handhold ing of SC/ST entrepreneurs may 
work well in improving the performance of this Scheme. Underutilization of funds 
is a serious cause of concern for the Committee; therefore, Ministry is advised to 
ensure full utilization of funds. 
(Para 85) 
 
Action Taken 
 
Interventions introduced under National SC -ST Hub are demand driven.  For 
wider outreach of the various interventions of Hub and subsequently increase the 
utilization of fund, various awareness campaigns are being organised. Inaddition, 
NSSH is leveraging t he network of 5,000+ Commons Service Centres (CSCs) 
Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) and 9,000 Post Offices for generating 
awareness of the Scheme among SC/ST entrepreneurs. 
 
Further, based on the Third -Party evaluation report, the scope of NSSH is 
proposed to be expanded viz., inclusion of services sector under SCLCSS, 
enhancement in financial assistance under various reimbursement interventions, 
distribution of latest  technology toolkits, reimbursement of registration fee of all 
Government promoted e-commerce, etc. All efforts will be made to ensure that the 
funds allocated for the Scheme are utilized fully. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
9. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should create an All -India 
Database of SC/ST entrepreneurs’ locations a nd vocations and share the same 
with CPSEs so that CPSEs can locate SC/ST units easily for availing their 
services. Also, the SC/ST Hub should run NSQF compliant skill development 
programmes for SC/ST technicians who could take contract jobs and services t hat 
CPSEs outsource. 
(Para 86) 
 
 
 

 
 
8 
 
Action Taken 
 
A database of more than 1,00,000 potential SC -ST MSEs has been created 
under National SC/ST Hub. The data is being shared with various CPSEs based on 
their product requirement on regular basis. With respect to NSQF compliant 
courses, the Ministry of MSME h as collaborated with various Govt. and 
autonomous training institutions such as MSME Tool Rooms / Technology 
Centers, Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI), NIELIT, CIPET, 
etc. Various skill development NSQF compliant training programs (both 
residential and non -residential type) are being conducted under the National         
SC-ST Hub. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
10. The trend under Public Procurement Policy has not been encouraging over 
the years. The Committee therefore, recommends that the t rend should be 
reversed and adequate steps should be taken by the Ministry to ensure fair 
participation of SC/ST MSEs in Public Procurement Policy.  The Committee also 
recommends that more special VDPs should be organized for SC/ST 
entrepreneurs for improvi ng their participation in Public Procurement Policy. 
The Ministry should also adopt handholding approach while promoting SC/ST 
entrepreneurs.   
(Para 87) 
 
Action Taken 
 
337 Special Vendor Development Programmes (SVDPs) have been organised 
with CPSEs having  participation of 10,554 SC/ST candidates across the country. 
Considering the challenges due to COVID -19 Pandemic, 91 online Vendors 
Development Programmes have been organized in FY 2020 -21, wherein 2743 
SC/ST candidates participated. Details of the SVDPs/ BSMs organized by NSSH 
offices are as follows:

Further, the eligible entrepreneurs are provided handholding support for

In addition to the above, for improving the participation of SC -ST MSEs in

(1) Taken up with GeM for introduction of social category filter on the GeM

Recommendation/Observation 
 
11. The Committee observes that many Schemes of the Ministry are not working 
satisfactorily in North Eastern Region and has a very negligible presence in these 
areas.  Even the number of ISEC issued under Khadi and Polyvastra are also not 
impressive. The Committee recommends that serious effo rts should be made by the 
Ministry to benefit the people of NER through its various Schemes with the help of 
State Governments particularly potential women and SC/ST entrepreneurs be 
encouraged to participate in the growth process. 
 
(Para 88) 
 
Action Taken 
 
Under the Scheme, "Establishment  of new Technology Centers/ Extension 
Centers”,20 Technology Centers and 100 Extension  Centers are being established

As far as six components of CLCS -TUS (ZED, Lean, Incubation, Design, 
IPR, Digital MSME) are concerned, efforts have been made with the help of all 
concerned stakeholders for SC/ST/women and NER entrepreneurs encouraged to 
participate as a part of the Scheme. 
 
To encourage the projects in NER & women and SC/ST entrepreneurs:

 For Industrial Estate & Flatted Factory Complex, the limit of GoI grant is

The Interest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate (ISEC) Scheme: 
a) ISEC Scheme was introduced in May 1977 to mobilize funds from the 
banking institutions to fill the gaps in the actual fund requirement and 
availability from budgetary sources. 
b) The Scheme is applicable for all registered Khadi Institutions/Coop 
Societies/Trusts under KVIC/KVIB. 
c) The Khadi Institutions shall pay 4% interest and the difference between 
the actual lending rate of interest minus 4% which will be borne by KVIC. 
d) ISEC limit is fixed for the Khadi Institutions based on their level of 
production and/or sales and the estimated requirement of funds in 
accordance with the prescribed pattern of assistance of KVIC to meet the 
working capital requirement.   
Reasons f or non -availment of 100% of ISEC issued by KVIC by Khadi 
Institutions: 
 
i. KVIC and banks were following different methods of assessing the 
working capital requirements of the KIs.  
ii. KVIC is assessing the Working Capital based on the target fixed on 
Production, Retail Sales, Wholesales, Vastragar, Raw Material and 
processing only, whereas, the banks are considering available opening 
inventory level of finished goods and credit facilities being extended by 
the trade creditors also.

27. The Committee hopes that the new classification of MSME would bring 
about positive changes in the MSME Sector. The Committee therefore, 
recommends that a study needs to be conducted to know the exact impact of 
COVID 19 Pandemic on the MSME sector and to as certain what benefits have 
accrued to the MSME sector by change of criteria for classification of MSMEs 
and introduction of various Schemes. The Committee may also be apprised about 
the findings of the study for perusal. 
 
(Para 3) 
Action Taken 
 
National Sm all Industries Corporation (NSIC) and the Khadi and Village 
Industries Commission (KVIC) have already done some studies to assess the 
impact of COVID-19 Pandemic on MSMEs. 
 
The study done by NSIC relates to the effect of COVID -19 on the 
beneficiaries of NSIC.  The major findings are as follows:- 
 
(i) 91% MSMEs were found to be functional. 
(ii) The five most critical problems faced by MSMEs are identified as 
Liquidity (55% units), Fresh Orders (17% units), Labour (9% units), 
Logistics (12% units) and availability of Raw Material (8% units.) 
The study conducted by the KVIC relates to the effect of Covid -19 on the 
beneficiaries under the PMEGP Scheme.  The findings of the s tudies are as 
follows:- 
(i) 88% of the beneficiaries of PMEGP Scheme reported that they were 
negatively affected due to COVID -19 while the remaining 12% 
stated that they were benefitted during Covid-19 Pandemic. 
 
(ii) Among the 88% who were affected, 57% stated that their units were 
shut down for some time during this period, while 30% reported drop 
in production and revenue. 

 
 
28 
 
(iii) Among the 12% who had benefitted, 65% stated that their business 
increased as they had units in retail and health sector and around 25% 
that their units benefitted as they were dealing with essential 
commodities or services.   
In addition, a dipstick study was conducted by the National Institute for  
Micro Small and Medium Enterprises  (NiMSME)  on credit  related issues , 
this reveals that the Hospitality and Tourism sectors have been adversely 
affected due to Covid-19 Pandemic. 
 
 
The Ministry has also commissioned a study on ‘Assessment of Sick/closed 
MSMEs,’ which will, inter -alia, include quantitative and qualitative effects of the 
Covid-19pandemic on sickness and closure of MSME units in the country. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 The Committee notes from the reply furnished by the Ministry that 
NSIC, KVIC & N IMSME had cond ucted the study to assess the impact  of 
COVID-19 pandemic on MSME Sector only. No study has been conducted to 
assess the benefits accrued to MSME Sect or due to the change in criteria for 
classification of MSMEs. The Committee, there, reiterates it’s 
recommendation and desires that the Committee may be apprised of the 
findings of the report.

Action Taken 
 
 
 
 
The Guarantee Emergency Credit Line (GECL) Scheme is implemented by 
the National Credit Guarantee Trust Company , which is under the administrative 
control of the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. The  
Ministry of  MSME is thus releasin g the funds for the corpus created for 
extending guarantees under this Scheme on the advice of the Department of  
Financial Services. The Scheme was earlier being implemented as the Emergency 
Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) by the Department of Financial Services. 
 
The Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) was announced as 
part of the AatmaNirbhar Bharat Package in 2020 with the objective to help 
MSMEs/small businesses to meet their operational liabilities and resume 
businesses in view of the distress caused by the COVID -19 crisis, by providing 
member lending institutions (MLIs) 100 percent guarantee against any losses 
suffered by them due to non -repayment of the ECLGS funding by borrowers. An 
overall ceiling of Rs. 3 lakh crores of guarantees was approved.  

 
 
30 
 
 
Since its launch, the ECLGS has undergone extensions and changes keeping 
in view of the impact of Covid on various sectors of the economy and the 
emerging needs. All these changes were made within the overall ceiling of the Rs. 
3 lakh crores guarantee cover.   In May 2021, on account of the disrupt ions caused 
by the second wave of the COVID 19 pandemic to businesses across various 
sectors of the economy, the Government has further enlarged the scope of ECLGS 
as under: 
i. Overall cap of admissible guarantee has been raised by Rs. 1.5 lakh crore - 
from 3 lakh crore to 4.5 lakh crore. 
ii. Launch of fourth component as ECLGS 4.0:  Provided 100% guarantee to 
MLIs for extending loans up to Rs. 2 crores to hospitals/nursing 
homes/clinics/medical colleges for setting up on -site oxygen generation 
plants. Interest rate under this is capped at 7.5%; 
iii. Extension in period of repayment to ECLGS borrowers who are eligible for 
restructuring as per RBI guidelines of 05.05.2021; 
iv. Additional ECLGS assistance  of up to 10% of the outstanding as on 
29.02.2020 to borrowers covered un der ECLGS 1.0, in tandem with 
restructuring as per RBI guidelines of 05.05.2021; 
v. Removal of ceiling of Rs. 500 crores of loan outstanding for eligibility under 
ECLGS 3.0  subject to maximum additional ECLGS assistance to each 
borrower being limited to 40% or Rs.200 crore, whichever is lower; 
vi. Civil Aviation sector  (scheduled and non -scheduled airlines, chartered flight 
operators, air ambulances and airports) made eligible under ECLGS 3.0;  
vii. Validity of ECLGS extended to 30.09.2021  or till guarantees for an amou nt 
of Rs. 4.5 lakh crore are issued 
The design of ECGLS provides flexibility to quickly respond to emerging 
needs, as has been evidenced by the introduction of ECLGS 2.0, 3.0 and 4.0 as 
well as changes as mentioned above, all of which were within available  headroom 
of Rs . 3 lakh crores. Currently, about Rs. 2.73 lakh crores (2 -7-2021) of loans 
have been sanctioned under ECLGS. Keeping in view the changes announced in 
the Scheme recently, extension of limit of one time restructuring to Rs. 50 crores 
by RBI o n 04.06.2021 and the continuing adverse impact of COVID on 
businesses, it was decided to enhance the existing overall guarantee limit of Rs. 3 
lakh crores to Rs. 4.50 lakh crores. At 15% default estimation, the additional 
requirement of corpus is worked out at Rs. 22, 500 crores. 
 
As per the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC), loans 
amounting to Rs 2.73 lakh crores have been sanctioned till 02.07.2021 out of

Action Taken (Reply to Para 48 and 49 same) 
 
Reasons for non -availment of 100% of the ISEC issued by KVIC by Khadi 
Institutions are as follows: 
 
i. KVIC and banks were following diff erent methods of assessing the 
working capital requirements of the KIs.  
ii. KVIC is assessing the Working Capital based on the target fixed on 
Production, Retail Sales, Wholesales, Vastragar, Raw Material and 
processing only, whereas, the banks are considering available opening 
inventory level of finished goods and credit facilities being extended by 
the trade creditors also. 
iii. Besides RBI guidelines each bank has issued internal guidelines also for 
the assessment of working capital based on the turn o ver with the 
institution’s contribution. 
iv. The recycling of working capital (i.e., operating cycle) is being assessed 
@ 16 months by KVIC, whereas the banks are calculating at a maximum 
of 4 months as applicable for other Textile Industries.  
v. Bankers are most ly considering fixing the C.C. limit @ 20% on the total 
turnover of the Khadi Institutions as that of extending loan facilities to the 
private/commercial establishments. 
vi. Bankers are expecting to realize sundry debtor’s dues by 90 days.  
vii. Bankers are insistin g to maintain 130% stock on hand for the C.C. 
limit fixed by them. 
viii. The banks are also insisting on collateral security for some cases and 
failure to furnish this by the KIs also results in lesser availment.  

 
 
39 
 
 
The above are some of the reasons for lower off take of the ISEC issued by 
KVIC in general and NEZ in particular. 
 
The matter is being examined in the Ministry to relook at the present 
methodology for estimation of ISEC value for Khadi Institutions. Efforts are being 
made to ensure uniformity between th e methodology used by KVIC to issue ISEC 
certificate and the working capital calculation methodology adopted by banks, to 
reduce the gap between ISEC being certified by KVIC and working capital 
amount sanctioned by banks. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation (Para 48) 
 
The Committee observes that different types of methodologies are 
being followed by KVIC and banks  in assessing the working capital 
requirements of the KIs , which is proving an impediment in issuance of 
ISECs for K hadi Institutions  throughout the country . This issue was also 
discussed in the Committee ’s meeting held on 8 th April, 2021 when banks 
CMDs were present in the meeting.  The Committee, therefore, recommends

methodology regarding the working capital  requirements of KIs which is 
acceptable to both for increasing the offtake of the Scheme and the number 
of ISECs  to the KIs .  The Committee feels that lack of awareness may be a 
reason for the gaps between number of ISEC issued by KVIC and working 
capital amount sanctioned by banks.   The Committee further recommends 
that Ministry should organize massive awareness campaigns through various 
modes available to popularize the Scheme among general public.  
 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation (Para 49) 
 
The Committee notes that the KVIC is assessing the recycling of 
working capital (working cycle) @ 16 months but on the other hand the

allocation of Rs. 150 crores was earmarked in BE 2020 -21 under the Hub. 
However, due to the Covid -19 pandemic, the off take under the interventions of 
Hub was not at the expected level. Further, facilitation of SC/ST MSEs for their 
participation in International as well as domestic exhibitions could not be made  
during the year. However, the entire allocation of Rs. 120 crores made in RE 
2020-21 under the Scheme has been utilized. 
 
In BE 2021 -22, an amount of Rs. 150 crores has been allocated under the 
National SC/ST Hub. Several modifications to make the Scheme more inclusive 
and effective have been proposed under the SFC Notes for its continuation in next 
financial cycle. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 The Committee observes that despite claims being made by the 
Ministry of the success of National SC -ST Hub Scheme, negligible results are 
being seen at the ground level. The National SC -ST Hub Scheme was 
launched with the aim of promoting entrepreneurship culture among 
marginalized sections of the society but the desired results are not being seen.  

 
 
45 
 
The proc urement from SC/ST entrepreneurs has remained around            
0.69 per cent for FY 2021 -22 as against 4 per cent annual sub -target set for 
central ministries, departments and PSUs to procure from SC/ST MSEs, as 
reported on SAMBANDH portal of the M/o MSME and there has been a 
continuous decline over the previous years. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that concrete steps should be taken by the Ministry to ensure 
adequate participation of SC /ST entrepreneurs in the Public Procurement 
Policy and meeting 4 per cent target for procurement  from SC/ST MSEs .  
Further, Ministry should also ensure to spend the budgetary allocations 
earmarked for National SC-ST Hub Scheme in time-bound manner to ensure 
optimum budget utilization. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
46 
 
CHAPTER-IV 
 
Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the 
Government are still awaited 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
43. The Committee was apprised by the Ministry that besides 219 Districts, 56 
Aspirational Districts have also been covered under SFURTI. The Committee 
recommends that more attention should be paid to target more and more 
Aspirational Districts across the country as this can immensely improve the socio -
economic conditions of the inhabitants in those districts and improve the human 
development index. The Ministry may coordinate with the state governments and 
with concerted efforts desired results may be achieved .  
(Para 55) 
 
Action Taken 
 
As on 30.4.2021, 65 clusters have been approved in Aspirational Districts.  
Nodal Agencies under SFURTI Scheme have been advised to explore the 
possibility of setting up more clusters in the Aspirational Districts.

Pune expressways and work is in progress for installing another 2 charging stations.  The

Recommendation/Observation 
2.            The future of the automobile Industry is going to be influenced by the next 
generation autonomous driving technology. The next generation aut onomous driving 
technology is currently in the development and testing phase in the developed nations. It 
would rather enhance road safety and reduce road accidents, pollutions and carbon 
emissions, fuel consumption, road congestion, make transportation ac cessible to all 
including disabled. The Committee has been informed that the autonomous vehicles are 
in different levels, with level 0 being the manual cars of today and level 5 the fully 

 3 
autonomous, self -driven vehicles. The Committee is aware of a few de merits of 
autonomous vehicles in Indian environment owing to the heavy traffic and poor road 
conditions, more so as it will affect the employment of Drivers. In India, some 
manufacturers are now introducing level 1 autonomous vehicle. OEMs are working on 
R&D and would be launching different levels of vehicles with autonomous functionality 
in the near future. The Indian automobile industry has a stake on the global Auto Sector 
and hence any lag may leave us behind in the race. To keep pace with the latest 
technology, the Committee expects that necessary initiative in this regard is taken to 
promote autonomous driving technology to compete with the international market trends. 
    
 (Para 38) 
Action Taken Replies 
Autonomous vehicles will be encouraged. 
In order  to ensure that Indian manufacturers keep pace with the Global auto 
manufacturers, the Automotive Industry Standards (AIS) Committee has already initiated 
the formulation work for the following aspects of autonomous driving technology viz., 
Auto Emergency Braking (AEB) for Commercial vehicles application, and Lane 
departure system.

take all out efforts to promote the development of Technical Platforms unde r the Capital

Action Taken Replies 
Department has embarked on innovative path to engender R&D in manufactu ring 
by developing six Technology Innovation Platforms which shall be   accelerators for 
making India self-reliant in various fields of the Capital Goods Sector with focus on 

 5

 Fuel Efficiency Regulation for Light, Medium and Heavy - Duty BS VI vehicles 
may also be implemented from 1st April, 2024.  
 OBD II Regulation for two Wheelers and three Whee lers scheduled for 1st April, 
2023 may be deferred and implemented in two phases, 1st Phase from 1st April, 2024 
and 2nd Phase from 1st April, 2026. 
 
(Para 37) 
 
 
 

 36 
Action Taken Replies 
It is informed that suggestions received directly from Automobiles Assoc iations 
regarding deferment in the emission regulations have been forwarded to the concerned 
Ministry/Department for favourable consideration.    Present recommendations of the 
Committee have also been shared with them. 
 
Background: 
 
(a)  India has submitte d its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) in 2015 for 
the implementation of Paris Agreement in the post 2020 period. The NDC has 8 goals, 
including 3 quantitative goals, one of which is: reduction in emission intensity of Gross 
Domestic Product (GDP) by 33% to 35% by 2030 from 2005 levels. 
(b) Government has set a target of reducing import of crude oil by 10% for the year 
2022. 
(c) Ministry is trying to align Indian automotive standards to European standards for 
enhancing India‟s global competitiveness. 
(d) There is a dire need to reduce air pollution. 
CAFÉ Norms (Fuel Efficiency for Passenger vehicles) 
 
In order to meet the global commitment, the Ministry of Power, under the Energy 
Conservation Act, issued notification S.O. 1072(e) 23 rd April 2015 to e nsure that motor 
vehicle types approved under Central Motor Vehicle Rules (CMVR) 1989 up to 3.5 tons 
gross vehicle weight follow the energy consumption standard for the purpose of 
manufacturing or importing for sale in the following manner:- 
 
 Each manufac turer shall comply with Energy consumption standard in the 
following phases: (i) The 1st phase was applicable from 1st April 2017 to 31st March 2022 
with a target CO 2 Emission of 13 gm/km. (ii) The second phase, effective from 1 st April 
2022, laid a target of CO2 emission equal to 113 gm/km. 
 
Therefore 7 years of preparation lead time was given to the auto manufacturers in mutual 
agreement with all the stake holders, including the automobile industry. 
 
Global Experience: 
The target of Japan for the year 2020 was 115gm/km. 
The European Union has set a target of 95gm/km for 2021. 
 

 37 
Fuel Efficiency norms for Light, Medium and Heavy Duty Motor Vehicles 
Fuel Efficiency norms have not been implemented so far. 
 
Inter-Ministerial Committee under MoPNG has already fin alized the fuel 
efficiency norms. However, due to BS VI and revision of axle loads, the correction 
factors have been finalized with the participation of the industry. It is under approval. 
 
Real Driving Emissions (RDE): 
To reduce emission performance gap o f vehicles between lab and real driving 
conditions, Real Driving Emission (RDE) regulation was introduced with Bharat Stage 
VI (BS VI) norms, vide GSR 889(E) dated 16 th Sept. 2016. India also made RDE 
measurement mandatory during type approval and COP (Con formity of production) 
applicable from 1 st April, 2020 for data collection and from 1 st April, 2023 for meeting 
Conformity factor (CF). Europe has made these regulations applicable from September, 
2017. Therefore, sufficient lead time has been given to the  automotive industry to meet 
the timeline. 
 
On Board Diagnostics 
 
On-board diagnostics („OBD‟) is essential for timely repair and maintenance of 
vehicle. It is required to review the list of devices monitored for electric circuit 
malfunctions, including excess emissions. 
 
OBD requirements for BS-VI compliant 2W in India 
OBD system specifications for two-wheelers have been included for the first time 
in the BS VI regulation in September 2016. 
 
India has introduced OBD -I for Wheelers from 1 st April 2020. The applicable 
requirements are circuit continuity checks, MIL (Malfunction Indicator Lamp) 
requirement, electrical disconnection of EVAP (Evaporative purge control) system and 
EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) monitoring. 
 
OBD-II goes a step ahead. Apart from O BD-I requirement, it proposes to include 
catalytic converter monitoring, misfire detection and oxygen sensor monitoring for 
deterioration along with OBD threshold emission requirements. The requirements of 2W 
OBD I and II are summarized in the table below:-

Due to global commitments, to reduce air pollution, to align with global standards

Recommendation/Observation 
40. The GST rates on automobiles are at the highest level of 28%. Indian industry 
and suppliers have invested significant resources to migrate to BS -VI. As far as two -
wheelers are concerned, in leapfrogging from BS -IV to BS -VI, Industry has recorded a 
35% increase in cost in the last quarters. Small engine size two -wheelers are used by a 
major population of self -employed, entrepreneurial common people. Hence there is need 
to consider the affordability for end -customer. Reduction in GST rate would help 
sustained growth in the industry and accelerate the adoption of BS -VI and improve GST 
collection accruing from increased sale. The Committee, therefore, recommends that to 
improve affordability of the customers and simultaneously boost the automobile sector, 
the GST rate on all segments may be reduced from 28% to 18%. The decreased GST rate 
would prove to be an impetus to enhance the sales and thereby, would offset the losses, if 
any, to the Exchequer kitty.  
(Para 39) 

 39 
Action Taken Replies 
To overcome the issu es faced by the automotive industry, Department had a 
meeting with leaders of the auto industry SIAM, ACMA and several OEMs 
manufacturers for suggestions. Department has forwarded the recommendation to the 
Department of Revenue for reduction of GST.

41. The Committee notes that presently, there is no parity in the Road Tax imposed by 
different States. The Committee has been informed that the MoRTH has been discussing 
this issue with States and is proposing an agenda of “One Natio n One Tax” as per the

benefit of the people across the country.

Revival and Mill Development Plan (RMDP)  of NEPA Ltd. which was slated to be

should be made on a priority basis to complete the RMDP of NEPA expeditiously. A 
compliance report on this aspect may be furnished to the Committee.  
(Para 90)

Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
1. Also the Committee was informed about the key observations of the study 
which was that the small businesses were worst hit by the economic fallout of Co vid-
19 Pandemic. Unprecedented lockdown and other containment measures have 
resulted in supply chain disruptions and massive demand drop especially for Micro 
units and significant economic losses in general to MSMEs. Further as per the 
survey data, 88 per cent of the beneficiaries of PMEGP units reported that they were 
negatively affected due to Covid -19 Pandemic and the remaining 12 per cent stated 
that they were not affected. In terms of beneficiaries (88 per cent) who were 
negatively affected, around 57 per cent stated that their units were shut down during 
this period, 30 per cent reported that there was drop in production and revenue, 28 
per cent stated issues pertaining to raw material availability or supply chain issues. 
In terms of beneficiaries (12 per cent) who were positively affected, around 65 per 
cent stated that there is an increase in business activity as they had units in retail 
and health sector, 53 per cent stated an increase in telephonic supply/delivery and 
around 25 per cent stated that their units were dealing with essential commodities or 
services. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take immediate 
suitable action to rescue the small business units from collapsing, by providing 
additional financial support, relaxation or w aiver of interest, marketing support,  
etc.  
(Para 50) 
Action taken 
 
The Reserve Bank has announced the following relief measures for MSMEs 
adversely affected by the outbreak of the pandemic:  
(i) Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector – Restructuring of 
Advances: With a view to facilitate meaningful restructuring of stressed MSME 
accounts a one -time restructuring of loans to MSMEs that were in default but 
‘standard’ as on January 1, 2019 , was permitted, without an asset classification 
downgrade, vide our circular dated January 1, 2019, subject to certain conditions. 
The scheme was extended vide circular dated February 11, 2020 to stressed MSMEs 
loans that were ‘standard’ as on January 1, 2020 subject to certain conditions 

 
 
3 
 
including implementation of restructuring by December 31, 2020. In view of the 
need to support the viable MSME entities on account of the fallout of COVID -19, 
the scheme has been extended for restructuring of advances whe re the borrower’s 
account was a ‘standard asset’ as on March 1, 2020 and aggregate exposure was up 
to Rs. 25 crore. The restructuring under this scheme had to be implemented by 
March 31, 2021. This scheme permits banks to upgrade such accounts as ‘standard  
asset’ upon implementation of the restructuring plan which may have slipped into 
NPA category between March 2, 2020 and date of implementation.  
 
(ii) Resolution Framework for COVID -19-related Stress: Stressed MSME units 
having exposure of more than Rs. 25 cror e may avail benefits under RBI circular 
dated August 6, 2020 on Resolution Framework for COVID -19-related Stress which 
has permitted a window under the Prudential Framework to enable the lenders to 
implement a resolution plan in respect of eligible corpora te exposures without 
change in ownership while classifying such exposures as standard subject to 
specified conditions. Under the guidelines, provisions have been made for inter alia 
allowing extension of the residual tenor of the loan, with or without paym ent 
moratorium, by a period not more than two years as well as providing additional 
funding based on viability considerations. 
 
Further, in view of the resurgence of Covid -19, the Reserve Bank has 
announced the Resolution Framework 2.0 dated May 05, 2021 s ubsequently revised 
on June 04, 2021 which permits lending institutions to restructure the advances to 
MSME borrowers, which could not be restructured under earlier schemes, without a 
downgrade in the asset classification subject to the conditions specifie d in the 
Resolution Framework 2.0. The facility is available to MSME borrowers having 
aggregate exposure, including non -fund based facilities, of all lending institutions 
not exceeding 50 core INR as on March 31, 2021 and shall have to be invoked by 
September 30, 2021. 
 
Even in respect of MSME accounts restructured under earlier schemes, 
lending institutions have been permitted, as a one -time measure, to review the 
working capital sanctioned limits and / or drawing power based on a reassessment of 
the working capital cycle, reduction of margins, etc. without the same being treated 
as restructuring. 
 

 
 
4 
 
(iii) Rescheduling of Payments and other reliefs on account of Covid -19 Pandemic 
under Covid-19 Regulatory Package– Term Loans and Working Capital Facilities 
 
a) All comm ercial banks (including regional rural banks, small finance banks 
and local area banks), co -operative banks, all -India Financial Institutions, and 
NBFCs (including housing finance companies and micro -finance institutions) were 
permitted to allow a moratorium of six months on payment of installments in respect 
of all term loans outstanding as on March 1, 2020. 
 
b) In respect of working capital facilities sanctioned in the form of cash 
credit/overdraft, lending institutions were permitted to allow a deferment of  six 
months on payment of interest in respect of all such facilities outstanding as on 
March 1, 2020. The accumulated interest for the period would be paid after the 
expiry of the deferment period. Alternatively, the lenders could convert the 
accumulated interest into a funded interest term loan payable by not later than March 
31, 2021. 
 
c) In respect of working capital facilities sanctioned in the form of cash 
credit/overdraft, lending institutions were allowed to recalculate drawing power by 
reducing margins and/or by reassessing the working capital cycle for the borrowers.  
 
(iv) Loans against Gold Ornaments and Jewellery for Non -Agricultural End-uses: 
Loan-to-value ratio (LTV) was temporarily increased from 75 per cent to 90 per cent 
till March 31, 2021 for loans  against gold ornaments and jewellery for non -
agricultural end -uses. Fresh gold loans sanctioned on and after April 1, 2021 shall 
attract LTV ratio of 75 per cent as hitherto. 
 
(v) Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS): Government of India 
has launched Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) for business 
including MSMEs and the scheme is being implemented by National Credit 
Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC). As credit facilities extended under the

10. The Committee is of the view that the 90 days limit fixed by RBI for classifying 
overdues of MSMEs should be increased to 180 days so that MSMEs are not 
constrained to divert their working capital towards servicing of their loan -
instalments and clearing th eir dues at the cost of normal business operations. This 
proposed change in the RBI guidelines will save a large number of MSMEs from 
turning sick or getting closed resulting in loss of economic activity and employment. 
It will also prevent avoidable class ification of bad debts and unwarranted litigation 
by banks, thereby saving the banks too, from losses.  
(Para 41) 
 
Action taken 
 
The extant asset classification norms of RBI which stipulate 90 -days past due 
(DPD) requirement for declaring an account as NPA  were issued based on the 
recommendations of the Financial Sector Reforms Committee (Chair: Shri  
Narasimham) after extensive deliberations and based on best international practices. 
Most of the jurisdictions around the world, particularly all the G20 count ries, follow 
the same norm of 90 days for classification as NPA, which has also been enshrined 
as part of Basel guidelines. 
 
The current norms constitute one of the key pillars of the prudential regulation 
and diluting the same will have broader financial stability implications. 
Classification of a borrower account as NPA by lending institutions is merely a 
formal, albeit delayed, recognition of the underlying stress in the borrower accounts 
and any dilution of the same will only delay the process of resolu tion of the stress in 
borrower accounts. Doing so will ultimately impair the financial health of the 
banking system and constrain their lending ability. 
 
Moreover, merely changing the criteria for recognition of an asset as non -
performing may not solve the financial stress associated with the exposure. 

 
 
19 
 
Resolution of financial stress involves recognition of stress as the first step, which 
may entail the lending institution having to recognize the losses incurred. 
 
Recommendation/Observation

12. The Committee notes that the production of Covid related medical and

Action taken 
 
For fight against Covid -19 pandemic, Tool Rooms & Technical Institutions 
have developed/manufactured various components/products  such as 
Sanitizers, Masks, Parts of PPE Kit, Corona testing kit, Box to sanitize office files 
and other articles using UV lights, accurate infrared thermometer, non -contact 
dispensers, Pulse -oximeter, prototype of Oxygen Generator, prototype of Non 
Invasive Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP)  type Ventilator  etc. Most of 
these items were supplied to various Central /State Gov ernment, offices, Bank, PSUs 
and Industries. Few items like Non -Invasive CPAP    type Ventilator, Automatic 
Hand Sanitizer Dispenser Machine, UV light based Sanitization Channel for 
material, Automatic sanitization channel etc. have been shared with 
MSMEs/Industries for domestic/indigenous production and marketing.  
 
MSME-DIs and Branch MSME -DIs have assisted and extended hand -holding 
support to many MSME units to manufacture PPE kits, Masks, Medical Oxygen, 
cloth Mask, N -95 Mask, sanitizer, sanitizer pump, Pl astic bottle pump and other 
auxiliary items. 
 
Based on the local needs and availability of raw materials, MSME -DIs 
prepared Project Profiles and provided to existing MSME units for their product 
expansion/diversification and prospective entrepreneurs for m anufacturing of 

 
 
21 
 
medical & auxiliary items like Mask, Sanitizers, Phenyl, Soap, Healthcare 
Garments, Pet Bottles, etc. Project Profiles thus prepared were uploaded in their

13. MSMEs are finding it difficult to procure raw material to run their businesses 
normally due to non -availability of raw materials. Moreover, a steep hike in the 
prices of raw material like steel etc. has adversely affected the business 
environment. The Committee recommends that the Public Sector Enterprises should 
not impose penalty or black list the MSMEs in the event of cancellation of orders by 
them since increase in prices of raw materials is a Force Majeure event, beyond the 
control of the MSMEs. Besides, the Government should also allow import of all steel 
materials based on cost and quality requirements at zero import duty (no anti -
dumping) and also ban export of iron ore and steel products for the time being. 
Better GDP growth can be realized only if value-added products are exported rather 
than raw materials. Further, GST -based funding is needed for MSMEs at marginal 
rates, which will encourage them to purchase raw materials easily.  
 
(Para 58) 
 

 
 
22 
 
Action taken 
 
Steel is a deregulated sector where prices are a function of demand and 
supply, global market conditions, trends in price of raw materials, logistics cost, 
power and fuel cost etc. The factors contributing to increase in price of steel over the 
last one ye ar include demand -supply mismatch following Covid -19 led lockdown, 
disruption in supply chains, logistics, availability of human resources, raw materials 
and working capital etc., reduced availability of steel across the globe during the 
pandemic leading t o global increase in iron ore and steel prices and reduced 
availability of iron ore domestically due to non -operationalization of working mines 
in Odisha post auction in March 2020. 
 
The Government has also taken steps to ramp up production of iron ore and  
steel to increase their domestic availability so as to offset the impact due to price 
which include increasing availability of iron ore through Mining and Mineral Policy 
reforms to enhance production and availability of iron ore, ramping up production 
and maximum capacity utilization by government mining companies, grant of 
permission to Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) to sell 25% fresh fines and 70 
Million Ton dumps and tailings, accelerating auction of iron -ore fines by SAIL and 
early operational ization of forfeited working mines of Odisha by the State and 
Central Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) etc. 
 
In Union Budget 2021-22, Customs Duty has been reduced uniformly to 7.5% 
on Semis, Flat and Long products of non -alloy, alloy and stainless steels . Further, to 
provide relief to metal re -cyclers, mostly MSMEs, BCD on steel scrap has been 
exempted for a period up to 31 stMarch 2022. In addition to the above, anti-dumping 
duty (ADD) and countervailing duty (CVD) on certain steel products have also been 
revoked / temporarily revoked. 
 
Keeping in view the overall interest of the domestic steel sector, blanket ban 
on imposition of Anti -dumping duty and complete ban on export of iron ore and 
steel may not be a feasible proposition in a de -regulated and diversified steel sector. 
Considering all aspects, Government makes required adjustments in Export/Import 
duty and takes safeguard measures from time to time.  
 
The Nationa l Steel Policy  (NSP), 2017 aims at inter -alia achieving a wider 
presence globally in value added/ high grade steel. The Government has approved a 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Specialty Steel to boost the domestic 

 
 
23 
 
production of ‘Specialty St eel’ and attract significant investment for production of 
‘Specialty Steel’ in the country. It will help the Indian steel industry mature in terms 
of technology as well as move up the value chain. 
 
Regarding GST based funding, some banks have started GST b ased credit 
scheme for the MSMEs where the MSME unit/borrower should have requisite 
registration under GST Act and it should have valid GST returns for a prescribed 
period which varies from Bank to Bank.  
 
Besides, Government has taken a slew of relief measures for the benefit of 
GST taxpayers, including for MSME units, so as to cope with the adverse effects 
of COVID-19 Pandemic. The list of such measures is placed at Annexure- A. 
 
Recommendation/Observation

Credit related issues have been largely deregulated, with freedom for banks to

Credit related issues have been largely deregulated, with freedom for banks

18. The Committee notes that, after the emergence of second wave of the Covid -
19 in April, 2021, the Government has recently announced ECLGS 4.0 with the 
Scheme period extended up to 30.9.2021. However, there has been no increase in 
the earmarked amount sanctioned under the Scheme. Keeping in view the efficacy of

Action taken 
  
The resurgence of COVID -19 pandemic in India in recent weeks and the 
associated containment measures adopted at local/regional levels created new 
uncertainties and impacted the nascent economic revival that was taking shape. In 
this environment the most vulnerable category of borrowers are individual 
borrowers, small businesses and MSMEs, for which, ECLGS, as a targeted policy 
response w as introduced by GoI. The ambit of ECLGS was expanded to provide 
some relief to the vulnerable sectors not covered earlier and also keeping in view the 
adverse impact of the second wave of Covid -19 on different sectors, the Cabinet in 
its meeting dated 30. 6.2021 has approved enhancement of the existing overall 
guarantee limit of Rs. 3 lakh crore to Rs. 4.50 lakh crore. 
  
Initially the scheme was launched to all eligible borrowers with opt -out clause. 
Later, in the subsequent versions of ECLGS i.e. ECLGS 2.0 , 3.0 & 4.0, the specific 
stressed sectors were included as per their enterprise business needs.

27 
 
less parameters of compliances etc. could help i n developing import substitution in

Ministry of MSME has designed and implemented  several schemes for

Rural Industry and Entrepreneurship (ASPIRE), Credit Guarantee Scheme

As on date, 18 incubators have been selected under the scheme. 734 startups

29

Building Awareness on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) For Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises.: During FY 2020 -21, 28 IP Facilitation Centres have been 
approved and 105 Patents/Trademarks have been reimbursed under the scheme.

Many of the schemes implemented by the Ministry of MSME caters to the

Recommendations/Observations in Respect of Which the Committee Has Not

Recommendation/Observation 
 
22. The Committee notes from the written replies furnished by the Ministry that no 
intensive study has been conducted by the Ministry of MSME to ascertain the actual 
losses suffered by the MSME Sector as a whole due to nationwide lockdown imposed 
by the Govern ment. More so, the second wave of the Pandemic exposed the 
vulnerabilities of MSMEs like never before and highlighted the problems faced by 
them such as delayed payments, high informality, low financial resilience, scarcity 
in raw material availability etc . The Committee, therefore, is of the opinion that a 
detailed study needs to be conducted to make an assessment of the actual losses 
suffered by the MSME Sector so as to chalk out an effective plan for revival of the 
MSME Sector, which has the potential to  contribute significantly in achieving the 
much coveted target of making India a $5 trillion economy.   
(Para 25) 
 
Action taken 
 
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) had assigned the task of 
conducting a National level evaluation of the PMEGP Scheme to Deloitte Touche 
Tohmatsu India LLP.  The agency had submitted the report in September, 2020.  
 
Key Observations:  
 
 Small businesses were hit by the economic fallout of COVID -19 pandemic. 
Lockdown and other containment measures resulted in supply chain 
disruptions and demand drop  especially for micro units.  The containment 
measures taken to check the spread of pandemic led to significant economic 
losses to MSME units. 
Units affected by COVID-19 pandemic: 
 

 
 
32 
 
As per the survey data 88% of the beneficia ries of PMEGP units reported that 
they were negatively affected due to COVID -19 and the remaining 12% stated that 
they were not affected. 
In terms of beneficiaries (88%) who were negatively affected around 57% 
stated that their units were shut down during this period, 30% reported that there was 
drop in production and revenue, 28% stated issues pertaining to raw material 
availability or supply chain issues.  
 
In terms of beneficiaries (12%) who were positively affected, around 65% 
stated that there is an increase in business activity as they had units in retail and 
health sector, 53% stated an increase in telephonic supply/delivery and around 25% 
stated that their units were dealing with essential commodities or services.  
 
Ministry of MSME has also initiated the process to conduct a study to assess 
the impact of change in classification of MSMEs. This study will also inter -alia 
focus on the actual losses suffer ed by the MSME sector due to Covid -19 pandemic. 
This study will also focus on impact of simplification of registration process, impact 
of inclusion of traders under the ambit of MSMEs and benefits accruing to the 
MSME sector due to introduction of various schemes under AatmaNirbhar Bharat in 
the background of COVID -19 Pandemic. The study has already been assigned to 
SIDBI.  Besides, A Quick Survey (836 responses) was recently conducted with the 
help of NI-MSME to assess the impact of MSMED Act, 2006.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee notes that the Report of the National Level Evaluation of 
the PMEGP Scheme assigned to Deloittee Touche Tohmatsu India was 
submitted to the Ministry in Septemb er, 2020. The Committee desires that the 
Action Take n on the Report may be shared with the Committee . The 
Committee further notes that the Ministry has initiated the process to conduct a 
study to assess the impact of change in classification of MSMEs t hrough SIDBI 
and a quick survey was recently conducted b y the Ministry with the help of NI-
MSME to assess the impact of MSMED Act, 2006. The Committee hopes that 
the report on the study would be complete d soon by SIDBI . The Committee 
further recommends that the action taken  on survey conducted by NI-MSME 
may also be shared with the Committee. 
 

 
 
33 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
23. The Committee is of the view that the M/o MSME may make all -out efforts to 
instil confidence in more women entrepreneurs to on -board the Udyam Portal. 
Likewise, majority of industrial sectors, including the ancillary ones as well as more

campaigns in the form of seminars/conferences in vernacular languages, 
advertisements in local dailies etc. to encourage the entrepreneurs, including women 
entrepreneurs, to file  Udyam Registration. As many as 8,96,167  women

organised around 583 programmes such as Industrial Motivation Campaign,

to encourage more women entrepreneurs to register in the Udyam Portal. MSME -
DIs are organizing nearly 200 similar programmes during FY 2021-22. 
 
In addition to the above, MSME -DIs encourage Women entrepreneurs in 
association with respective Women Industries Association and SHGs in the States to 
register themselves as Self Help Groups in Udyam Portal, to get  the benefits of 
various schemes of the Government. 
 
Monthly meetings are being organized with Women Entrepreneurs’ 
Associations regularly to create awareness / assistance for Udyam registration.  
 
Publicity about various schemes through social media like F acebook, Twitter, 
Youtube etc., have been initiated.

English and Hindi and translated into other regional languages and uploaded on the 

 
 
34 
 
website of Office of DC (MSME) and websites o f respective MSME -Development 
Institutes.

Under NLAP, 126 field offices of the Ministry conducted the programme in more 
than 630 colleges throughout the country encompassing more than 70,000 
participants. Besides, Ministry is regularly releasing campaigns on social media to 
promote its schemes, activities, Udyam Registration etc. 
 
As part of the programme ‘Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana’ under 
Coir Vikas  Yojana, the Coir Board is conducting various field level awareness 
programmes like EDPs, Workshops, Seminars, Conferences, etc. for the coir

programmes, the Board is giving awareness to the entrepreneurs and encouraging 
them for getting registered under the Udyam Portal to enable them to avail the

Recommendation/Observation 
 
24. It has been observed that after reclassification of criteria of MSMEs and 
subsequent introduction of Udyam Registration Portal, less number of MSMEs have 
got registered on the new Udyam Portal since 1st July, 2020. It appears that MSMEs 
feel better off wit hout registration as the compliance costs would be much greater 
than the benefits that would accrue post registration. Besides, without registration,

35 
 
Action taken 
 
The three biggest incentives for registration on the UDYAM portal are:  
(i) to avail benefits of schemes implemented by the Ministry of MSME;  
(ii) to avail benefits of schemes of State Governments/UTs. e.g. Haryana, Bihar, 
Maharashtra, Jharkhand, etc.; 
(iii) to avail benefits of Priority Sector Lending (PSL),  RBI has issued a circular 
dated 21stAugust, 2020, wherein the lending under PSL category is linked to Udyam 
Registration. 
 
The erstwhile system of Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum was started in the year 
2015 and till 30 thJune, 2020, there were 1.02 crore registrations under it. The new 
registration process was started w.e.f 01.07.2021, and in a span of around 1 year and 
3 months, the total number of registrations have crossed 52 lakh, i.e. more than 
12,000 registrations per day.  
 
National Level Awareness Programme (NLAP), was organised by the Minis try 
on the Schemes/Initiatives/Activities of the Ministry from 17.02.2020 to 09.03.2020 
through its field offices across the country. Under NLAP, 126 field offices of this

26. The Committee observes that the directions issued by the Government of India 
to its agencies and CPSEs to release payments to MSMEs within 45 days has yielded 
some positive results and outstanding payments have been released by PSUs/CPSEs 

 
 
38 
 
to MSMEs. However, it is observed that many PSUs/CPSEs have still not released 
payments. Though there is a provision for 1 per cent penalty on delayed payments, 
in practice, the penalty clause is seldom invoked, which encourages the defaulting 
entities to flout the prescribed t imeline. The Committee recommends that strict 
provisions against delayed payments need to be put in place to ensure timely release

capital/credit requirements.

Provisions related to delayed payments to MSEs are included in Chapter V of 
MSMED Act, 2006. As per Section 16 of the Act, if a buyer fails to make payment

at three times of the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
The malaise of delayed payments for goods supplied and services 
rendered continues to plague the growth of the MSME Sector in India . The 
Government’s initiatives in this direction yielded some positive results but still 
a huge amount is pending on the CPSEs. The Committee , therefore,  
recommends that  provisions contained in Chapter V of MSMED Act, 2006 
should be strictly implemented in lette r and spirit for quick redressal of the 
issue of delayed payments to MSMEs by CPSEs , which will ultimately 
strengthen MSME Sector in the country.   
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
27. The Committee also recommends that necessary guidelines should be issued 
for mandatory reporting of the delayed/pending payments (beyond 45 days) to

manner.

acceptance of the goods or services, to submit a half yearly return to the Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs stating the amount of payments due and the reasons of the delay.

meant for a specific set of borrowers. This might be one of the reasons for low

30. It has also been observed that MSMEs do not publish their invoices on TReDS 
platform despite having the registration  due to unsaid pressure from corporate 
(buyers). Further , it is seen that corporate (buyers) do not approve the published 
invoices of MSMEs on TReDS platform, which defies the sole purpose of the 
platform, as Banks cannot fund such invoices. The Committee is of the view that 
every tax invoice raised by GST registered MSMEs should reflect automatically on 
the respective TReDS platforms. After the delivery of Services or Goods, within a 
certain number of days, the corporate must accept or reject the automatic ally 
published invoice of MSMEs. After the stipulated period, the published invoice 
should be deemed accepted and should be available for banks to provide fund to 
MSMEs. If the CPSEs rejects any invoice, a mandatory clarification must be sought 
which shoul d be visible to Banks and respective MSMEs. Consequently, MSMEs 
would be encouraged to get themselves registered on GST and TReDS Platforms as 
their invoices would automatically get published on TReDS which would open the 
doors for them to have access to e asy and cheaper funds. It would also provide 
significant business potential for banks due to rise in number of invoices available 
on TReDS. The Committee feels that it would also make CPSEs responsible and 
cautious while rejecting any invoice raised by MSM Es and help them financially in 
this critical juncture. The proposal if implemented, would thereby, become a win -
win situation to MSMEs, CPSEs and Banks as each one of them are likely to benefit.   
 
(Para 62) 
Action taken 
 
Besides the registration of CPSEs on TReDS platform, Department of Public 
Enterprises (DPE) has also advised all the administrative Ministries/ Departments on 
17.10.2018 to direct their CPSEs to ensure MSE vendors registered with CPSEs are 
also to be registered on TReDS platform.  
 
CPSEs have also been advised to have a system with facility for uploading of 
bills of vendors and payment through the portal. 
 

 
 
43

administered by Ministry of MSME . Section 2 (ii) of the Act provides that in case 
no objection is made by the buyer regarding acceptance of goods and services 
within 15 days from the date of delivery of the goods or the rendering of services, 
it would be treated as “deemed acceptance”. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee would like to know the outcome of the advisory issued to the 
CPSEs and what steps have been taken by the CPSEs in respect of uploading

the Ministry in a time -bound manner and also the Committee should be

Recommendation/Observation 
 
31. Ecommerce is growing at a very fast pace and it is expected to grow to 
US$200 billion by 2026. It plays a major role in streamlining business processes 
right from receiving a product order, to managing deliveries, keeping tr ack of stock 
and even analyzing consumer feedback and data. The future is the age of online 
marketing. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry may study the working of 
big ecommerce players to adopt efficient and successful practices for strengtheni ng 
the entry and survival of MSMEs in ecommerce. Through ecommerce, MSMEs not 
only can sell in indigenous markets but also get into markets abroad, which will 
definitely be a booster for MSMEs.   
(Para 84) 
 
Action taken 
 
To promote e -Commerce among MSMEs following initiatives have been 
taken by Ministry of MSME. 
 National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) has created MSME Global Mart 
(www.msmemart.com) a global business to business (B2B) portal facilitating online 
marketing support to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) by way of 
increased visibility on internet, showcasing their product & services 24X7 , 
connecting buyers & suppliers,  providing trade leads & keyword based Tender 

 
 
44 
 
alerts etc. to grow their bu siness. Services of MSME mart not only focus towards 
increasing the visibility of products globally but also focus on providing value added 
services and relevant information to support MSMEs throughout the business cycle 
& it acts as online platform / mark et place for connecting buyers and suppliers for 
providing them open market access. Mobile app is also functional and already 
downloaded by 43,100 users. The portal has been on-boarded on UMANG Portal. 
 New portal of KVIC ( www.ekhadiindia.com) has been launched on 01.01.2021

Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
Ecommerce has enab led MSMEs to widen their market reach, create 
more jobs and boost their revenues and this trend is expected to continue  in the 
future also  exponentially. Through e -commerce, even small MSMEs get to 
showcase their products across the globe without spending much on expansion 
or changing their location. E -commerce has immensely helped MSMEs to get 
rid of the business hurdles  and acquiring a larger customer base and increase 
in their revenue.  The Committee recommends that Ministry should pay special 
attention to this tool of new age which is capturing the market rapidly .  
Ministry should study the methodology and tactics of big e -commerce giants 
like Flipkart & Amazon and adopt the same for Indian MSME Sector for its 
empowerment.  The Committee feels that MSMEs in India have the potential to 
compete with global players by using the power of e -commerce and they can 
grow in leaps and bounds in coming future.

Measures taken so far to support MSMEs 
 
A. Atmanirbhar Bharat  
1. ₹ 3 lakh crores Collateral -free Automatic Loans for Businesses, including 
MSMEs: The Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) has been 
formulated as a relief measure to MSMEs by providing them additional funding 
of up to ₹ 3 lakh crore in the form of a fully guaranteed emergency credit line. 
Borrowers with up to ₹ 25 crore outstanding and ₹ 100 crore turnover are 
eligible. This scheme provides 100 per cent credit guarantee cover to Banks and 
NBFCs on principal and interest. No guarantee fee, no fresh collateral is required.  
2. ₹20,000 crore Subordinate D ebt for Stressed MSMEs : Provision made for ₹ 
20,000 crore subordinate debt for MSMEs which are NPAs or are stressed. 
Government to support them with ₹ 4,000 crore to Credit Guarantee Trust for 
Micro and Small enterprises (CGTMSE). Banks are expected to pro vide the 
subordinate-debt to promoters of such MSMEs equal to 15 per cent of the 
existing stake in the unit subject to a maximum of ₹ 75 lakhs.  
3. ₹ 50,000 crores equity infusion through MSME Fund of Funds:  Government to 
set up a Fund of Funds with a corpus of ₹ 10,000 crore that will provide equity 
funding support for MSMEs. The Fund of Funds shall be operated through a 
mother and a few daughter funds. It will provide equity funding for viable 
MSMEs. This scheme will help MSMEs to expand its size and capacit y and will 
also encourages them to get listed on stock exchanges.  
4. New definition of MSME: Low threshold in MSME definition have created a fear 
among MSMEs of graduating out of the benefits. Hence, government has revised 
definition of MSME by raising the I nvestment limit. An additional criteria of 
turnover has been introduced and distinction between manufacturing and service 
sector stands removed.  
5. Global tenders to be disallowed upto ₹ 200 crores:  General Financial Rules 
(GFR) of the Government amended to disallow global tender enquiries in 
government procurement of goods and services of value of less than ₹ 200 crores. 
This is a step in support of the Make in India initiative and will promote MSMEs 
to grow.  
6. Other Measures for MSMEs: e-market linkage for M SMEs to act as a 
replacement for trade fairs and exhibitions. MSME receivables from Government 

 
 
48 
 
and CPSEs to be released in 45 days. This would help MSMEs to solve the 
problems of marketing and liquidity.

worth ₹ 5,204 crore has been issued with the objective to help MSMEs to carry 
on their business activities without pay cuts and layoffs in these challenging 
times. 
8. Relief of ₹ 1500 crores to MUDRA - Shishu loans: GoI to provide Intere st 
subvention of 2 per cent to prompt payees for a period of 12 months. Small 
business under MUDRA to be benefited.

further enhancement of Ease of Doing business through Insolvency a nd 
Bankruptcy Code (IBC) related measures which include (a). raising of the

of Heavy Industries on the recommendations co ntained in the Committee‟s Three  Hundred and 
Third Report on Downturn in Automobile Sector – Its Impact and Measure s for Revival 
pertaining to Ministry of Heavy Industries. 
 
2.  Action Taken Replies  have been recei ved from the Ministry  of Heavy Industries  in 
respect of the recommenda tions contained in the 303 th Report. These have been categorized as 
follows: 
 
Chapter-I-      The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry. 
  Para: 30, 68, 69, 71, 80, 81 and 86 (Total: 07)

  Para: 49, 50, 51, 52 and 77 (Total: 05)
