Action  Taken  Rerport
Modified guidelines of the PMRY Scheme under implementation since 1.4.99 do not provide for any minimum
stipulation for projects under industry sector. Despite the enhancement in the projects cost from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 2 lakh
in the revised guidelines, the average loaning under the Scheme continues to be around Rs. 60,000/- per beneficiary,
rendering it difficult to set up any industrial activity out of this. In addition the setting up of projects under industry
sector requires getting power connections, license and NOCs etc. Hence, few people are going into for projects under
industry sector. The self-employment  can mean self employed ventures business and service sectors also. Average
employment generation per unit set up under the PMRY is 1.5% which can either be from industry, service or business
sectors. During the Review Meetings of the PMRY it was deliberated that one of the reasons for rejection of
application/non disbursal of loan was the tendency to adhere the minimum loaning from the industry sector. Since the
aim of the Scheme is to provide self employment, it has been decided by the Government to withdraw the 50% ceiling
on projects from the indsutry sector.
Further Recommendations
The Committee notes the reply given by the Ministry of A & R I. The Committee, however, is still of the opinion
that in the absence of industry, no asset is created. Since PMRY has been brought under the Ministry of A & R I, it
would be appropriate to give a thought as to how to promote Agro and Rural industries under the scheme.

Action Taken Rerport
The Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana was launched on 2 nd Oct. 93. During 1993-94, the scheme was in operation
only in urban areas of the country. Subsequently, the scheme is being implemented in both urban as well as rural areas
of the country. The guidelines of the scheme do not prescribe that PMRY is basically a Rural programme only.
Similarly, the guidelines of the scheme envisage 22.5 per cent reservation for SC/STs. It is also stipulated in the
guidelines that in case sufficient SC/ST candidates are not available, the State Governments are competent to consider
the applications from other categories.
Article 40 (Chapter VI) of the persons with the disabilities (equal opportunities and fully participation) Act 1995
provide for not less than 3% reservation for disabled in all poverty alleviation programmes. Since PMRY is an
emloyment generation programme and not a poverty alleviation programme, the provision of 3 per cent reservation for
physically disabled persons does not apply to PMRY Scheme.
Further Recommendations
While noting the reply of the Ministry of A&RI, the Committee is disturbed to know that sufficient number of
applications are not coming from the SC/ST candidates. The Committee recommends that awareness programmes about
the PMRY should be regularly held amongst SC/ST candidates. The Committee also recommends that reservations for
disabled perons in the matter of granting loans under PMRY should be included.

Generation Programme (REGP). The volume of finance is also higher. The Committee desires that in view of the
parallel schemes attracting more attention of entrepreneurs, PMRY scheme norms may be revised so as to make it more
popular. PMRY scheme may be implemented through Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) also to increase the coverage.
Subsidy in  Kerala
4.10 In order to attract more and more educated youth to the scheme, the Committee feels:
               lSubsidy ceiling of Rs. 7500 be raised to Rs. 15,000 subject to a minimum of 15 per cent.
               lThe ceiling on income (Rs. 40,000) may be enhanced to Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 60,000 so as to enlarge the
selection zone.
Action Taken Rerport
The 'Review Committee' constituted to review the implementation of the PMRY Scheme has submitted its
recommendations including that on enhancement of subsidy.
The enhancement in the subsidy ceiling has financial implications and hence require approval from Expenditure
Finance Committee (EFC) and Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
The RBI has opined that it is not possible to permit the Regional Rural Banks to participate in the implemenatation
of the PMRY due to the weak financial position of these banks. The suggestion regarding enhancement on ceiling in the
family income under the PMRY is under consideration of the Government of India.
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE AT A GLANCE
The Committee recommends that the Central Government should pursue with State Governments to prepare State
speeches publicity module based on infrastructures and marketability of products.     (Para 2.15)
The Committee notes the evasive reply that the RBI has stated that it is not possible for them to undertake such a
study without giving any adequate and valid reasons. The Committee feels that in the interest of the country the RBI
should undertake a study to overcome the difficulties of the banks as well as the best possible way to identify viable
projects.                                                                                                                   (Paras 2.22 & 4.1)
The Committee notes the reply given by the Ministry of A&RI. The Committee, however, is still of the option that
in the absence of industry, no asset is creatable. Since PMRY has been brought under the Ministry of A&RI, it would be
appropriate to give a thought as to how to promote agro and rural industries under the scheme.(Para 3.22)

While noting the replies of the Ministry of A&RI the Committee is disturbed to know that sufficient number of

authorised  by the Committee, hereby present this One Hundred –tenth  Report on the Action Taken by the Government
on the recommendations contained in  the  Committee ' s  86
th Report  on Performance review of Metal  Scrap Trade
Corporation Limited (MSTC).
 
2.         The Committee examined and considered the Action Taken Notes on recommendations contained in the
Committee’s 86th Report on Performance review of Metal Scrap Trade Corporation Limited (MSTC).
 
3.         The Committee at its meeting held on  17
th December,  2002 considered and adopted the Report.
 
 
 
NEW DELHI;
December 17, 2002
DR.P.C. ALEXANDER
Chairman
Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Industry
 
REPORT
 
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Steel on the Recommendations
contained in the 86
TH Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry Report on
Performance review of Metal  Scrap Trade Corporation Limited (MSTC).
2.         Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Steel   in respect of the   recommendations
contained in the Report.   These have been categorized as follows:
 
Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry of Steel  
 
(Chapter - I).
Recommendations:- 3.1.6 ,  3.1.7, 3.2.5, 3.2.6, 3.2.7, 4.7, 5.4, 6.3, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.6,  and 12.7
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Government's replies :
(Chapter - II)
Recommendations:- 2.3,  and 3.3.2,
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted replies of the Ministry of Steel   :.
(Chapter - III).
Recommendations:- 7.4, 7.5,  8.6 and 11.2
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which  final replies of the  Ministry of Steel   have not been received.
(Chapter - IV).
Recommendations:-  9.2, 10.6, 10.7, 10.8, 10.9 ,13.1.2, 13.2.2, 13.2.3,  13.3.2 and  13.3.3.
3.         The Committee is pleased to observe that  the   Ministry of Steel has accepted its  recommendations  as 
mentioned in Chapter –I of the  Report.

convinced  with the logic and explanation  advocated by the Ministry of  Steel  and therefore   does not want to  pursue 
further .
5.         The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementations  of recommendations contained in  Chapter-

these recommendations.

replies or couched its language in  vague terms like  noted for compliance/guidance therefore, the Committee desires 
that the Ministry of Steel would furnish Action Taken Notes in  respects of recommendation categorized   in Chapter-
IV  in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the Committee.
7.            Observations/recommendations of the Committee  are given in Chapter (V)

CHAPTER - I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS  WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
 
           
Recommendations ( Para 3.1.6 and 3.1.7)  
 
MAIN ACTIVITIES
 
3.1.6    The Committee understands the compelling circumstances under which the  MSTC changed its focus of
activities from acting as a selling agent of SAIL to that of maximizing direct marketing (DM) when MSTC got de-
linked from SAIL in 1993.   The Committee appreciates the change in strategy in post-decanalised phase of imports.  
The Committee is pleased to observe the performance of MSTC in direct marketing and hopes that an all out efforts
would be taken by MSTC management to strengthen the marketing activities to improve upon financial performance to
a new commanding heights.
 
3.1.7    The Committee understands the problems being faced by MSTC in carrying out business in a situation when
demand for melting scrap is going down due to increased production of HBI and also because of setting up of scrap
disposal unit-set up by PSUs and other Government departments, MSTC management has to chalk out ‘new strategy’ to
combat the situation.  The Committee feels that provided the Ministry of Steel adhere to the principle of generating an
atmosphere of inter-PSU cooperation and take concrete steps towards assisting MSTC in procuring work-order from
Government PSU, the problems of MSTC could be sorted out to a great extent.  The Committee may be apprised about
the action taken by the Ministry in this direction.
 
Action Taken
 
The observations of the committee have been noted. Marketing activities of the Company have been further
strengthened. In 2001-02, International Marketing Division had achieved sales of Rs.413 crore as against Rs.274 crore
achieved in 2000-01. In 2002-03, in the first six months itself the volume of sales has crossed Rs.600 crore mark.
Financial results have also improved accordingly.
In order to further strengthen the marketing activities, MSTC has installed an e-auction portal and the company
has already registered about 400 customers.  To assist MSTC in procuring work-order from the PSUs, Ministry has also
addressed all PSUs under Ministry of Steel to use the services of MSTC vide letter No.9(13)/2002-MF dated 22.11.02.
KIOCL (Kudremukh Iron Ore Company Limited) has reported using e.auction of MSTC in case of two lots, in its letter
vide No.D.O.No.D(C)/2002  dated 3.12.02 to Ministry of Steel

Recommendations ( Para 3.2.5, 3.2.6,  and 3.2.7 )  
 
INTERNATIONAL MARKETING
 
3.2.5    The Committee is pleased to note the performance of MSTC in international marketing and appreciates the
strategy of MSTC management for enlarging its import basket in post decanalised phase to compete with other private
parties engaged in similar business.
 
3.2.6    The Committee feels that with the revival of steel industry and undergoing process of strengthening of anti-
dumping the prospect of MSTC in international market would lead to opening of new avenues.
 
3.2.7    The Committee further hopes that MSTC management would chalk out strategy to ensure its survival while
working in adverse condition caused because of lower demand for scrap due to change in charge-mix-owingto increased
availability of DRI and sponge iron.   MSTC has also to learn how to respond and work in a competitive environment.
 
Action Taken
 
The observations/feelings of the committee have been noted.   MSTC is already working successfully in a
competitive environment. In 2001-02, International Marketing Division had achieved sales of Rs. 413 crore as against
Rs. 274 crore achieved in 2000-01. In 2002-03, the volume of sales has crossed Rs.600 crore in the first six months.
Financial results have also improved accordingly.
 
Recommendations  ( Para 4.7)
 
MODERNISATION, RESTRUCTURING AND EXPANSION PROGRAMMES OF MSTC.
 
The Committee notes the steps taken by MSTC management in the field of modernization, restructuring and
expansion programmes of MSTC.  The Committee is of the view that although MSTC is not engaged in the process of
production and is a trading company, however, steps taken towards modernization and restructuring would help in
improving its operational efficiency and managerial effectiveness.  The Committee is of the firm view that
modernization in the process and system of working of the company would have a definite bearing on the physical and
financial performance of the company.  The steps taken to modernize and restructure the communication and expansion
in the domestic as well as international marketing Division would yield positive fruits in the functioning of the
company, the Committee feels so.   The Committee further feels that the efforts made on the part of MSTC management
for enlarging import basket would add to the profitability of the company.
 
Action Taken
 
            The views expressed by the Committee have been noted. 
            With a view to modernize and restructure its operations the company has started an e-auction portal which has
started hosting its tenders on the web-site and E-mail facility has been installed in all branches and regions.   These
measures have already resulted in an improvement in physical and financial performance.
            Some measure of restructuring has been done by merging the purchase & sales transactions both in the domestic
and international trade areas under a common marketing group.  
            The company has also confirmed that measures to enhance the export basket have led to greater profitability.
 
Recommendations ( Para 5.4) 
 
PERFORMANCE OF MSTC
           
            The Committee observes that the activities of MSTC has undergone noticeable change with the changing
scenario of steel industry, change in the Government policy i.e. perspective.   The MSTC which acted earlier as a selling

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

agency for SAIL in respect of their melting scrap arising, has started to carry the business with the other Government
PSU, SAIL started selling melting scrap directly.    MSTC went, rightly, for strengthening of Direct-marketing when the
Government policy stood for de- canalisation of import.  Although the performance of MSTC suffered to some extent
during this phase of tumultuous change, however, it is the managerial skill, which led MSTC for changing business
gear, and it is the concerted employees commitment which has got a bearing on the physical and financial performance
of the company.   The Committee acclaims the performance of MSTC and hopes that an all out effort on the part of the
management and employees would continue to improve the financial performance of the company to a new zenith.    
                                                                          
 
 
Action Taken
 
            Management as well as employees of MSTC are trying to put in their best to further improve the financial
performance of the company.
Recommendations ( Para 6.3)  
 
 MOU RATING OF THE COMPANY
 
6.3       The Committee observes that MSTC is coming out of the woods and doing excellent performance as is reflected
from MOU rating as awarded by Department of Public Enterprises after taking into various parameters of performance
into consideration.   The Committee wishes its best for MSTC for continuing its excellent performance in forthcoming
years and hopes that MOU system would always act as a catalyst to improve the physical and financial performance of
the company.                                          
 
Action Taken
 
            MSTC is thankful to the Committee for their good wishes and is confident of earning excellent MOU rating in
the years to come.
 
Recommendations ( Para 12.3, 12.4, 12.5,12.6, 12.7) 
 
SWOT ANALYSIS OF MSTC
 
12.3     The Committee observes that MSTC management has given due accordance to the significance of SWOT
analysis in the general working of the company.  The Committee appreciates MSTC management for adhering to the
basic principles and practice of management.   The efforts of re-defining of SWOT analysis on the part of MSTC
management to a praise-worthy step and the Committee hopes that MSTC management would continue to re-orient its
SWOT – analysis as per changing industrial and economic scenario and chalk out its further strategy as per the  outcome
of SWOT analysis.           
                                                           
12.4     The Committee is of the opinion that MSTC management should take advantage of its strength as the company
has minimal fixed overheads expenditure due to optimum manpower with expertise from SAIL equipped with modern
telecommunication and computer.   The Committee is pleased to note that MSTC has good track record for executing
contracts due to its goodwill in the domestic and international market.  Banking upon its company, goodwill/track-
record, MSTC management should make efforts to enhance its market share in domestic as well as international market.
                                                                                                                       
 12.5-   The Committee opines that with the induction of liberalization policy bureaucratic procedures and regulation has
been done away with.  However, MSTC management in tandem with the Ministry of Steel should point out in the ATN
of the present Report the bureaucratic hurdles and Government control having adverse imports on the marketing
capacity of MSTC.   The Committee is of the opinion that MSTC management should have a re-look on the areas of
weakness i.e. induction of latest technological developments, streamlining of the main activities positioning of right
man at the right place in right time, redrafting of corporate goal in the internal market etc.

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA

12.6     The Committee recommends that MSTC management would explore ways and means to capitalize on
opportunities for better financial performance of the Company and it is being hoped that the Ministry of Steel would
extend all possible help to MSTC in this regard.    MSTC management may explore new governess for activities of the
company and consequent changes in the object clearance of the company in order to infect synergy in the overall
working of the company.                                
 
12.7     The Committee further recommends that MSTC management should chalk out strategy for getting rid of threats
being faced by the company.   MSTC management may undertake required steps to inject resilience in the working of
the company in order to combat risk and undertake new works in open and competitive environment.                            
Action Taken
 
Regular updation of the Corporate Plan is indeed necessary and will be taken up in due course by the Company.
The Corporate Plan of the Company was broken down into three phases
                                                Years
            Short-term             -            2001-3
            Mid-term            -            2003-7
            Long-term            -            2007-12
           
It is hoped that most of the goals of the short-term plan will be achieved. While certain goals will be exceeded,
there may be a partial shortfall in goals in certain areas. Revision of the Corporate Plan will be taken up towards the end
of the financial year ending 31.3.2003.
MSTC is making continuous efforts to enhance its market share in the domestic as well as international market,
which is substantiated by the growth in the physical performance of the company for the last five years.
There are no specific bureaucratic hurdles impeding the work of MSTC. In any case, its operations are governed
by commercial considerations approved by the Board of Directors. In fact the status of the Company as a Public Sector
Undertaking enhances its credibility and performance capability because credibility is crucial for a trading house.
Furthermore the support from the Ministry gives the Company an added boost in its domestic marketing operations
particularly with other PSUs and Government Organisations.
            Advice given by the Committee for exploring latest technology for improved performance and also for chalking
out a strategy for getting rid of threats being faced by the Company would be given due attention.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
CHAPTER –II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE
 
Recommendation (Para 2.3)
 
CAPITAL STRUCTURE
 
2.3       The Committee notes that the company has an authorized Capital of Rs. 5 crore and paid up capital of Rs.2.20
crore as on 31.3.2001 of which approximately 90 per cent of the shares are held by the President of India and the
balance 10 per cent by the members of Steel Furnace Association of India and Iron & Steel Scrap Association of India
and others.  The Committee recommends that MSTC management would take every step to ensure that capital
restructuring of MSTC take place in such a way that return on investment (ROI) is maximum.
 
Action Taken

At the moment the Company is having no debt. There is also no plan to make any infusion of fresh capital.
Under the circumstances, there is no immediate plan of capital restructuring. However, as and when this is done, due
attention will be paid to the point made by the committee.
 
Recommendations ( Para 3.3.2)  
 
MSTC AS A HOLDING COMPANY.
 
3.3.2    The Committee notes the activities and responsibility of MSTC as a holding company.
 
Action Taken
 
            No recommendation has been made.
 
 
CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT
ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY OF STEEL
 
Recommendations ( Para 7.4 and  7.5)  
 
Projects/Schemes/Diversification Plans and Financial Requirements.
 
7.4       The Committee is pleased to note that MSTC management is giving due consideration to diversification plans
and entering into joint ventures.   The Committee is of the opinion that in the prevailing market Competitive era,
diversification of activities and projection of business through partnership/joint ventures has almost become a corporate
culture.   MSTC is moving in the right direction by adopting the canons of modern days business practice.   The
Committee hopes that MSTC, whether in existing structure i.e.as a PSU or in the post divested phase would continue its
efforts towards adopting the prevailing precepts and strategy in accordance with changing market scenario.
                                                                                                             
7.5       The Committee notes that financial provisions for completion of plans/schemes of MSTC and at the same time
hopes that all the plans and schemes would be completed without time and cost overrun.           
                                                           
Action Taken
 
Of the Rs.30 crore planned to be spent during 10
th 5-year plan, Rs.14.85 crore have already been invested in
FSNL which is included in BE for 2002-03.  As a technical investment, the Company has also acquired debentures
worth Rs.15.80 crore in Tirumala Rerolling Mills Pvt. Ltd. 
 
While it is MSTC’s hope to emerge as an international trading house, the size of the company (only 280 people),
the low capital base of the company (Rs.2.20 crore – paid up capital) etc. naturally impose a limit.   In trading, ability to
take financial risk and bulking of purchases are important factors.   It is envisaged that the company will continue to
grow but slowly and shall have to depend more on developing its infrastructure for growth.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
            The Committee is pleased to note that  MSTC  has  already  invested in Ferro Scrap Nigam Ltd. (FSNL)  to the
tune of Rs.14.85 crore earmarked in BE for 2002-03 out of  the  fund of Rs. 30.00 crore plan to be spent during  Tenth
Five  Year  Plan.  The Committee further notes that the Company has also acquired debentures worth Rs.15.80 crore in
Tirumala   Re-rolling Mills Pvt. Ltd.  The Committee observes that MSTC,  slowly but  steadily, is sailing through  the 
prevailing market competition  in the  liberalized and globalised  economy.  However, the Committee is of the view  
that   MSTC management may undertake  concrete steps  to widen  the capital base of company.  It is further  advised

that  adequate  steps may also be undertaken  for development of infrastructure  for growth .   The Committee further
recommends that   MSTC management should chalkout  strategy  for optimization of manpower  so that the small size
of the company should not come on to the way of company to emerge as an international trading house.
Recommendations ( Para 8.6 )  
 
OUTSTANDING ISSUES BETWEEN MSTC AND M/S. HARSCO CORPORATION INC. USA AND ISSUE OF
DISINVESTMENT.
 
8.6       The Committee observes that all on-going disputes between MSTC and its partner M/s. Harsco Corporation Inc.
USA should be resolved with the good offices of Ministry of Steel and SBI caps should evaluate the value of shares of
FSNL to facilitate the negotiation process at the earliest.   So far as the disinvestment of 100 per cent Government
shareholdings in MSTC through a strategic sale is concerned the committee desires that the Department of
Disinvestment may, in line with decision taken in regard to disinvestment of NALCO and MOIL, consider to give
MSTC employees/an opportunity to purchase atleast 5 per cent share in MSTC as a measure to allay fears among
employees and generate a sense of organizational belongings and commitment among employees.                                 
                                                                                   
Action Taken
 
The outstanding issues between MSTC and M/s Harsco Corporation Inc. USA have been resolved             and
the 40% shares held by M/s. Harsco Corporation in the subsidiary company Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited have since been
acquired by MSTC on 31.8.02 at a price of Rs.14.85 crores.
 
The suggestion of the Committee for giving MSTC employees the opportunity to purchase at least 5% of its
shares has been sent to Department of Disinvestment for consideration.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee is pleased to note that  the outstanding issues between MSTC and M/s Harsco Corporation  Inc.
USA have been resolved amicably and the 40% shares held by M/s Harsco Corporation in  the subsidiary company
Ferro Scrap Nigam Ltd.   have since been acquired by MSTC on 31.8.02  at a price of Rs.14.85 crores.  The Committee
feels that  the measures  undertaken   would  have a definite tangible  impact on  the physical and  financial 
performance company. 
 
The Committee, however, desires that Ministry of Steel should apprise the Committee  as soon as  the Ministry 
of Steel   receives the response/opinion of the Department of disinvestment  on the issue of giving MSTC employees an
opportunity to purchase    at least 5 per  cent  of its shares when  the company feels selected  for hundred percent
disinvestment.   
           
Recommendations ( Para 11.2)  
 
HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT OF MSTC
 
11.2     The Committee notes that there is no surplus manpower in MSTC at the moment and MSTC is managing in its
activities with a total manpower of 280.  The Committee is pleased to note that MSTC management is adopting the
strategy of redeployment of manpower in order to have optimum utilization of manpower.  The Committee hopes that
MSTC is adhering to the principle of right man at right place at right time which would certainly help in improving the
performance of the company.   The Committee also expects that MSTC management would examine the labour
productivity in term of turnover/Sales /profit and human resource as per requirement.                
Action Taken
 
The strategy of redeployment includes proper placement of personnel as well as the requisite training in order to
ensure optimum utilization of manpower and enhance their productivity. This strategy has apparently succeeded because
the per capita turnover/ sales/profit have been increasing for the last 5 years without any major change in the manpower.

Recommendations ( Para 9.2)
 
INTERIM TURN AROUND PLAN
 
9.2       The Committee recommends that MSTC management should continue with the interim turnaround plan to
improve further the financial performance of MSTC.  The committee is pleased to note that the measure of
diversification of imported basket has a positive bearing on the performance of MSTC and hopes that introduction of e-
auction for domestic marketing Division would go a long way in improving further the physical and financial
performance of the company.   
                                   
Action Taken
 
            The e-auction portal which has been launched in June, 2002 appears to have created a favourable impact in the
market and it is hoped that e-auction would go a long way in improving further the physical and financial performance
of the company.
 
Recommendations ( Para 10.6,10.7, 10.8 and 10.9)  
 
 PROCUREMENT OF WORK ORDER FROM SAIL, RINL AND RAILWAYS
 
10.6     The Committee recommends that MSTC management should strive its best to procure work order from SAIL,
RINL and Railways.   The Committee desires that MSTC management should also approach steel units in private sector
for work-order.   The Committee hopes that introduction of E-auction portal by MSTC management would help MSTC
to procure work-order from all around.
                                     
10.7     The Committee is of the firm view that the concept of inter-PSUs co-operation should be advocated by the
Ministry of Steel to lend a helping hand to other PSUs in the areas of mutual interest.  In this regard the Ministry of
Steel may act promptly as a facilitator and help MSTC in the procurement of work-order from SAIL and RINL.             
                                                                                                           
10.8     The Committee further recommends that MSTC management and the Ministry of Steel would continue to take
up follow up action with the Ministry of Railways (Railway Board) on continuous and regular basis for procurement of
work order.   The Committee desires that the Railway Board should give due consideration to the request of MSTC
management by giving preference to MSTC.                                                           
 
10.9      The Committee desires that the Ministry of Steel in its Action Taken Note of the present Report would furnish

13.1     Sales Tax Structure
 
13.1.2    The Committee understands the problems being faced by trading organization due to prevalence of multi-point
tax structure.   Therefore, the Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Steel should take up the matter with the
Ministry of Finance and State Governments.   The proposal of uniform system of VAT and one point tax may be
examined and if found feasible, steps in this regard may be taken at the earliest.

REQUIREMENT OF SUBMISSION OF END-USE CERTIFICATES FOR IMPORTED MELTING SCRAP
 
13.2.2                The Committee is of the opinion that the Government should evolve alternative effective mechanism to
check the misuse of scrap imported for melting, being used for re-rolling.
 
13.2.3                The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should approach the Ministry of Finance

of end use certificate by the actual users’ and in case of default, a certain penalty may be imposed on the defaulter.   The

REPORT
Alloy Steel Plant
 
 
 Alloy Steel Plant, a pioneer in the production of alloy and special steel in India, is located at Durgapur, District
Burdwan in the state of West Bengal . Alloy Steels Plant was commissioned in mid 1967 with the objective of
producing and developing various grades of alloy and special steels required by the country.  The plant was designed 
and  engineered by M/s  M.N.  Dastur & Co.  and the production know-how was obtained from M/s Atlas Steel,
Canada.  The integrated production in ASP   commenced from December, 1968 .  The  ingot  steel capacity of the plant
was further augmented by 60.00 tonnes per year by installation of  50 tonnes  arc  furnace with conditioning facilities
and by utilising the second shift of the blooming and  billet mill.  The expansion was completed in March, 1988.  The
capacity of the  plant  has since been expanded from  1,60,000 tpa to 2,60,000  tpa of liquid steel and 1,83,000 tonnes of
saleable steel.    Since its inception, Alloy Steels Plant has not only met the demands of its customers, it has also been
successful in developing many special categories of products required by strategic sectors.  However, despite a much
superior quality edge over its competitors, ASP is facing stiff competition  in the market for selling its products  due to
high cost of production  and  the plant is running loss  on the continuous basis. 
1.2       During the course  of interaction with the Sub-Committee-I,  in the meeting of the Sub-Committee  held  on 14
th
March, 2002,  the Secretary, Ministry of Steel, expressed his concern over  ASP's   performance :-
" The performance of ASP  continues to be disturbing .  It continuous   to make losses.  It is  generally assessed that  in
the prevailing market situation, with the  kind of   technology  and age of equipment that the ASP  has, it would
continue to be a  loss-making unit.  The  disinvestment of ASP is part of the  business   restructuring process of SAIL. 
The Steel Authority has invited bids for  disinvestment. They have invited expressions of interest, but, as of now, the 
assessment is that  there  are no takers.  It is again indicative of the fact that on SAIL's   commercial judgement, ASP is
a loss-making company.  It is something   that the market seems to affirm, because, as  I  said, there has been no 
response to the  advertisement for expressions of interest."
1.3       The Secretary, the Ministry of Steel, further added :-
" There may be  other units which are  on the margin   and with   a change in technology and market conditions,
perhaps, a particular  loss-making unit may turn  into a  profit -making unit.  But  this assessment, unfortunately, is not
right, as far as ASP is concerned."
1.4       The   Committee believes that the Secretary, Ministry of Steel has reasons to express concern over the
operational status of Alloy Steel Plant (ASP).  ASP is facing all odds.  The plant has suffered huge accumulated loss, is
incapable of utilising installed capacity and facilities available, scale of production is unviable, financial performance  is
dwindling,  cost of production is uncompetitive   and it has lost its market.  The disinvestment effect failed as
`Expression of  Interest'  (EOI )  has   evoked  no   response.  Government agencies are not coming forward to help the
plant out.  The performance of plant in the past has been gloomy and at presents the plant is at moribund stage.  The
Committee is of the opinion that the plant may reach to the  point of no return unless a comprehensively considered
revival package is undertaken to improve the operational efficiency   of the plant under  guided   supervision for the
ultimate survival and sustenance of the plant.

10.0
          Major problems faced by ASP and solution:
 
10.1          The sub-committee was informed that ASP is facing following problems:-
 
i                       Alloy Steels Plant is fundamentally un-competitive because of its  location, low quality of assets and
outdated technology.
ii                     Production at ASP is dependent on the uneconomical low power EAF  route and most of its equipment
is old.
iii                    The market demand for alloy and special steels  in India has stagnated at around 1.4-15 mt over the last
five years and the capacity utilization continues to   be  less than 50 percent  .  The market is high 
fragmented among various small players and ASP'S  market share  is  only 6 percent .
iv                   ASP has a business disadvantage  (vis-à-vis its competitors) in its location in the eastern region, while
nearly 60 percent  of the market demand is from southern and western regions.  ASP has a freight cost
disadvantage vis-à-vis a south based supplier.
v
                     ASP has lost volume steadily, as the requirement of inter-plant transfers have come down, on account of
economic considerations.
vi                   High manpower cost and high overheads.
 
10.2     As a result of inherent problems being faced by ASP, the plant has the trend of decreasing sales realization due
to high variable cost of production   compared to the competitors. SAIL is finding it very difficult to fund the losses of
Alloy Steel Plant, since SAIL'S overall financial performance itself is uncomfortable.
 
10.3     The Committee observes that the problems being faced by ASP are deeply- rooted  and pose the real threat for
the survival and sustenance of the   plant   under the prevailing environment.  There are the   reasons to believe that

16.0
          Disinvestment  of ASP
 
16.1            Considering  ASP’s financial performance   in the  past  and no  strong possibility of  improvement,
divestment  of ASP would have helped  SAIL in reducing its financial burden.   Accordingly, with the approval of GOI,
an advertisement inviting  EOI  was issued on 26.6.0 . The last date for receipt    of EOI  was 24
th August, 2001. 
However, the advertisement for inviting  EOI  has  evoked no response from any interested bidders.  Therefore, in view
of the above, it can be concluded   divestment  of ASP is not a feasible proposition. Given the accumulated losses by
ASP and its current performance, the divestment process has not attracted interest from any suitable bidder.  Hence, as
of now, the divestment possibility may be taken as closed.  The matter was  discussed in the last meeting of Committee
of Secretaries  (COS)   has   also noted that the divestment of ASP does not  appear   feasible  in the near  future and has
recommended that  all options  in this regard may be  worked out for consideration of CCEA. In view  of the fact that
the divestment of ASP does not  appear   feasible  in the near  future,  it has now been decided to follow a 2 pronged
strategy   vis.,
 
i
           Special thrust on reducing manpower; and
ii         To reduce level of operations at ASP, based on market conditions/financial aspects
 
16.2.    The Committee understands that, considering ASP's financial performance in the past and no strong possibility
of improvement, in future ASP is proving a nuisance SAIL in general and a burden on government's treasures. 
Therefore, efforts were made for divestment of ASP.  However, market proved much more prudent and Expression of
Interest (EOI) evoked   no response for purchasing the ailing plant of SAIL.  ASP is dwindling further, SAIL is not in a
position to invest on ASP , and Government   is not in a position to inject `new lease of life'  to the plant, which seems to
be at the  moribund stage.
 
16.3.    The Committee welcomes the two pronged strategy i.e. rationalisation of manpower and scaling down
production as per market demand.  The Committee hopes that strategy undertaken would improve operational efficiency
of ASP.

          Steps required for Revitalization of operational efficiency of ASP
 
19.1     The Committee is of the opinion that Alloy Steels Plant is a  pioneer in the production of stainless steel in India,
and   its products are  being  used by the Defence, Railway, Space Research Organisations, Nuclear Power Plants .
When India was debarred to import alloy steels required for Bofors Cannon Shells during Kargil conflict and high
quality special stainless steel required for  Atomic Research Centres ,after the Nuclear Test at Pokhran, it was ASP,
which  came forward to produce all these materials required at the moment of national crisis. Therefore, the Committee
feels that it would  be a national loss if ASP, a holder of ISO-9002 Certificate , is thrown away.

19.2          Merger of DSP and ASP
 
The Committee views thatthe close proximity of Alloy Steels Plant and Durgapur Steel Plant, under the same
organisations – SAIL, is a matter of great advantage. ASP is utilizing scrap skull, C. O. gas, electricity,  water, dolomite,
oxygen from DSP.  It also utilises Hot Metal/Liquid Steel, Ingot, Blooms & Billets as input materials. The two sister
plants of SAIL are having common township and Hospital, under the control of same Managing Director. Therefore ,
the Committee feels that the possibility of merger of DSP and ASP may be explored . This plant could be made more
cost effective by utilizing the in-house facilities of the two SAIL Plants, ASP & DSP. This requires  more close
supervision and effective co-ordination. This should not be a difficult job since the two plants are under the control of
same Managing Director.  What is needed, is the will of SAIL to run both the Plants, making best use of the technical
arrangements already prevailing to make both the Plants economically viable.
 
19.3     The suggestion of R&D, SAIL, to install an AOD at ASP for improving quality of stainless steel and EMS at
concast shop for production of Defence & Automobile requirements, should be examined The other suggestion of
technical experts like Dastur & Co. to install a Billet Caster, Wire Rod Mill and modernize the Forge Shop , may be
taken into  consideration .
 
19.4     The Sub-Committee was apprised of the fact that after installation of continuous shop in various steel plants, the
availability of mild steel scrap has drastically gone down.  ASP's requirement of scrap from different plants is 10,000
MT per month.  Following is the need from sister plants to sustain production level.
            1. Bokaro Steel Plant :   4500 MT
            2. Durgapur Steel Plant:    5500 MT
19.5     The special steels produced in integrated steel plant is very cost effective.  In ASP, is also exploring the
possibility of getting the inputs from Durgapur Steel Plant in the form of ingots/Basic Oxygen Furnace Liquid
steel/Rolled or Cast Billet & Blooms to the tune of 6000 MT per month.  At present it is at the level of 1500 T per
month. This is being perused at various levels in SAIL and  they  are sure to get this support within SAIL.
 
19.6
          Utilizing inputs from DSP like liquid steel  
 
The Committee is of the view that  to reduce the cost of production of ASP products, a substantial quantity of
ASP customer’s need can be meted out by utilizing inputs from DSP like liquid steel made through BOF route as well as
Ingots, Bloom and Billets.  The Committee hopes production of ASP may be carried on  with close co-ordination with
Durgapur Steel Plant.  With transfer of liquid steel from DSP to the tune of yearly 50,000 MT monthly 4500 MT.  To
facilitate the transfer of this Steel, necessary arrangement may  be made.
 
19.7          Installation of two numbers of E.M.S. in the CCS
 
The  installation of two numbers of E.M.S. in the CCS, which is essential for regaining lost market in the
automobile sectors of the Eastern Region , may be examined.
 
19.8     Use of DSP-ASP route
Electric Arc Steel making is a costly process which should   be sparingly used  at  ASP.  ASP should utilize
ASP's finishing facilities to produce around 90,000 tonnes of steel from DSP-ASP route per annum to make a cost
effective contribution. 
19.9            Nominal   Investment
ASP has a large potential in production of high quality  forgings   upto 12,000  TPA.  A nominal   investment to
augment the Unit in order to bring in high returns can be considered on priority. An  investment  of around Rs.2-3
Crores can enlarge product- mix as per market requirement .

The operational efficiency of both the production units viz Plate Mill & Bar Mill should be evaluated, and if

Alloy Steels  Plant  is a major supplier of steel products to Defence, Railways and almost all the important
Government Engineering establishments like BHEL,NTPC, CIL, GAIL, BARC, DMRL etc. use ASP's product   to the

Enterprises or on lowest bidders.  The purchase preference should be given to the  ASP keeping in view  high products
quality.  Since the Department  of Public Enterprise has extended  the  Purchase  Preference  Policy upto 31.3.04 , the
Ministry of Steel should take the  opportunity   to bag orders  from the other   PSUs to  surmount  the present difficult 
situation through which Steel PSUs are  passing .
 
OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE AT A GLANCE
 
Operational Status of Alloy Steel Plant (ASP)
 
            The   Committee believes that the Secretary, Ministry of Steel has reasons to express concern over the
operational status of Alloy Steel Plant (ASP)  .  ASP is facing all odds.  The plant has suffered huge accumulated loss, is
incapable of utilising installed capacity and facilities available, scale of production is unviable, financial performance  is
dwindling,  cost of production is uncompetitive   and it has lost its market.  The disinvestment effect failed as `
Expression of  Interest'  (EOI )  has   evoked  no   response.  Government agencies are not coming forward to help the
plant out.  The performance of plant in the past has been gloomy and at presents the plant is at moribund stage.  The
Committee is of the opinion that the plant may reach to the  point of no return unless a comprehensively considered
revival package is undertaken  to improve the operational efficiency   of the plant under  guided   supervision  for the
ultimate survival  and  sustenance of the plant.
( Para : 1.4)
Capital Structure
            The Committee is perturbed to note the huge accumulated loss of ASP.  The huge accumulated loss i.e. to the
tune of Rs. 1184.00 crores is a testimony to the fact that the pervious management failed to act promptly.
( Para :  2.3   )
Facilities available at ASP
            The Committee, while noting the facilities available at ASP, is constrained to express its concern over the under-
utilisation of facilities available at ASP.  Reasons for under-utilisation may be of different nature, i.e. varying   from
general recession in steel industry to specific and inherent problems of plant. Some of the   reasons might seems
justified   and might be well defended by   stating that, factors forming the reasons, were beyond the control of
management, the other reasons might be pointed out, could be dwindling market demand   of  ASP's  product.  However,
the   facts remains that   elaborate facilities is available at ASP and expansion programme   in ASP was completed as
late as March, 1988 and   infrastructure facilities of the plant has   since been expanded from 1,60,000 tpa to 2,60,000
tpa of liquid Steel and 1,83,000.  The Committee is perturbed to observe that investment on expansion projects in ASP
was made without proper techno-economic consideration. Expansion projects in ASP were bereft of cost-benefits
analysis, the Committee feels.
( Para : 3.3  )
Product Range
 
            The Committee feels that, since ASP  has elaborate facilities, it is but natural that the plant has the  basic
facilities to produce wide range of products  for a number of customers such as Engineering, Railways, Defence and
Automobile Sector.  But the irony of state of affairs in ASP is that the facilities available at ASP is gathering  dust and
the  wide  range  of products available  at ASP remained a mere expression on paper ,  as the so-called esteemed 
customers  of  ASP has turned their back to the  ASP product due to cost  disadvantages.  Therefore, the production in
ASP has, accordingly, been confined as per market demand.
( Para :  4.3   )
Scale of Production

            The Committee is of the opinion that the production level in ASP is, itself an indicator to the fact as how
improper planning in regard to enhancing the ASP 's capacity  from 1,60,000 tpa  to 2,60,000  tpa of liquid steel and
1,83,000  tonnes of saleable steel in March, 1988 led to misappropriation  of public  purse.  The plant failed to make
optimum   utilisation of installed capacity, the Committee observes.  Its a glaring example  of error of judgement.  It
might be well concluded that the  then decision -makers and the management  made a  blunder and  went  for the 
expansion  programme without  taking  into consideration the  techno-economic viability of the  plant.
( Para :  5.3 )
Sales performance
 
            The Committee observes that the plant has the capacity of  making 1,83,000 tonnes of saleable steel but the
actual sales remained confined to 134.9, 96.00 and 80.6 thousand tonnes during 1998-99, 1999-2000 and 2001-02,
respectively, which raises  a question mark on the economic  prudence  of decision maker of the time.  During 2001-02,
ASP is likely to sell 85,00 tonnes of Alloy Steel against rated capacity of  1,83,000 tonnes which works out to be 46
percent  .  The major orders received from PSUs  by ASP are  from Railway, Defence, BHEL, and steel plants.  In the
recent past, Railway and Defence,  have both curtailed their procurement and they are resourcing  their  requirement
from supplies other than PSUs also.
( Para : 6.2 )
Financial Performance of ASP
 
            The Committee views that, it is but  natural, that a plant which is not making optimum utilisation of facilities
available at site, neither  makes  full use of its installed capacity and which has  lost its market, can not  be expected to
perform better  on the financial   front.  ASP is incurring losses year after year and there is  no hope left  for
improvement in its performance, as the plant faces  indomitable problems.  The Committee is  of the  further view that
Government should make a final decision in regard to ASP at the earliest   as ASP is proving a burden  on public purse.
( Para : 7.3  )
 
            The reasons, as advocatd by the Ministry of Steel for deteriorating physical and financial performance of ASP,
makes the Committee to recall the proverb that  "misfortune never comes alone ", as the prevailing  conditions  in ASP
are  the major  stumbling block  for better  functioning of the plant.  The Plant, in itself , is in a dilapidated    condition 
and the Committee is dismayed, not only for the dwindling financial performance of ASP  but also for the  plant which
is gradually  but surely marching   towards sad demise.
( Para : 7.5  )
Cost of Production
 
            The Committee recommends that ASP management may undertake massive measures for cost-reduction  in the
production of the items
( Para : 8.3  )
Cost control measure
 
            The Committee appreciates the efforts made by ASP management for making a savings of Rs.5.00 crore during
2000-01.  The Committee hopes that such efforts would continue in future.
( Para : 9.2 )
Major problems faced by ASP and solution:
 
            The Committee observes that the problems being faced by ASP are deeply- rooted and pose the real threat for
the survival and sustenance of the   plant   under the prevailing environment.  There are the   reasons to believe that
ASP  plant is fundamentally  un-competitive because of its location, (ASP has  a business   disadvantage  vis-à-vis its
competitors  because  of its location in the   eastern region, while    nearly 60%  of the market demand is from Southern
and  Western regions  and  therefore, ASP has a freight cost  disadvantages vis-a-vis  a south based suppliers),  low
quality  of assets  and mounting  loss and liability ( against a net  fixed assets  of Rs.130.00 crore and current assets of
Rs.242.00 crores,   the plant has the  current liabilities to the tune of  Rs.212.00  crores and huge  accumulated loss to
the extent of Rs.1184.00 crore),   outdated-technology                      ( uneconomical  low  power EAF  route)  and

loggerheads for the viability  of the plant.  ASP, because of its high variable cost of production, is facing the problem of
decreasing sales realisation.  And since SAIL, itself,  is passing through  rough financial phase and its financial
performance, itself is  uncomfortable, SAIL is not coming forward for the  rescuing  act  of ASP.
( Para : 10.3  )

            The Committee recommends that ASP management for enhancing its market share may undertake concrete
efforts.  SAIL should help ASP in procurement of work-order from Railway, Defence, BHEL and other Steel plant.

            The Committee notes   the budgetary provision for ASP as earmarked for 2002-03 and hopes that schemes
undertaken would help ASP in improving its operational efficiency.

            The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should examine the proposal of upgradation of

may  facilitate ASP for  arranging  required  fund either from SAIL, on commercial borrowings on Government's 
guarantee.
( Para : 13.3)
Rationalisation of Manpower
 
            The Committee feels that rationalisation of manpower is   an absolute necessity in ASP    to reduce the element
of labour-cost component.  The programme of rationalisation of manpower should be completed in a time bound
manner and without any delay.
( Para : 14.5  )
SWOT ( Strength, Weakness, Opportunities, Threats)  analysis of ASP
 
            The Committee feels that ASP has failed, miserably, in taking advantage   of its strength , at appropriate time . 
ASP is not in a position to avail of its opportunities because of high cost of production as the finishing   facilities are not
cost   effective which   put ACP at disadvantage in matching international   cost and quality in the production of 
stainless steel and  other steel plants  are producing carbon construction steel at a lower cost.  Taking stock of SWOT  -
analysis , the Committee is of the opinion that the plant is heading towards a point of no  return.
( Para :  15.2 )
Disinvestment  of ASP
 
            The Committee understands that, considering ASP's financial performance in the past and no strong possibility
of improvement, in future ASP is proving a nuisance to SAIL's  in general and burden on government's treasure. 
Therefore, efforts were made for divestment of ASP.  However, market proved much more prudent and Expression of
Interest (EOI) evoked   no response for purchasing the ailing plant of SAIL.  ASP is dwindling further, SAIL is not in a
position to invest  , and Government   is not in a position to inject `new lease of life ' to the plant, which seems to be at
the  moribund stage.
( Para : 16.2 )

Objectives of Modernisation.

Recommendations ( Para 11.3  )
 
Further Modernisation and Restructuring for technology Upgradation
 
   The Committee recommends that the DSP management should push ahead, without delay, the issue of further
upgradation in DSP in regard to Bloom Caster with ladle furnace, New Finishing Mill, Introduction of coal dust
injection and Introduction of SGP for BF-2 for revenue generation and improvement in environment.  The Committee

is being considered.
 
Recommendations ( Para  12.2   )
  Conversion of CC Billets into finished products.
 
The Committee understands that almost 55 percent of DSP’s production comprises of semis, which are low contributory
items and fetch lower realization.  The product-mix of DSP is unfavourable and is affecting the profitability of DSP. 
The Committee recommends that DSP Management should chalk out a necessary course of plan for converting CC
Billets into finished products through conversion agents.  The Committee hopes that SAIL should lend its helping hand
to DSP management in chalking out the plan and proposing the same to Ministry of Steel, as the same would help DSP
in improving its physical and financial performance.

Recommendations ( Para  6.2 )  
 
Long-term Corporate Plan of RINL
 
The Committee notes the long-term Corporate Plan of RINL to increase its capacity to 10 million tonnes
(envisaging production of 7.0 million tonnes by 2013-14 and 10 million tonnes by 2019-20) with addition of production
units in both primary and finishing zones.  In this context, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should
examine the proposal of RINL management to enhance the  capacity of the plant and, if found feasible, the Ministry of
Steel should help RINL management   for arranging commercial borrowings.  However, it may be noted that the
capacity  expansion programme in steel sector should be well examined, keeping in view of  prevailing over supply in
steel market.  Therefore, the expansion programme  should be backed by intensification of diversification of product
range in order to be a dominant player in the market.
 
Action Taken
 
Ministry notes the observation of the Committee and will look at further capacity expansion of VSP, hoping the
national and international demand for its products and its long term interests.
 
Recommendations ( Para 7.5   ) 
 
RINL- On the profit- making track
 
The Committee observes that RINL is gradually,  but surely, marching ahead on the profit making track.  The
plant is already in the position of making cash profit and the Committee hopes that the plant, with excellent capacity
utilisation  and skilled and devoted work force, would soon start making net profit.
 
Action Taken
 
The Ministry notes the observations of the Committee and wishes to inform the Committee that as per tentative
financial results available for the first half of the current financial year the company has already registered a net profit of
Rs.125 crores. 
 
Recommendations ( Para 7.6  )  
 
Operational efficiency of RINL
 
                        The Committee recommends that RINL managements should intensify its efforts i.e., increase in
operational efficiency, enhance in capacity utilisation, adopt cost control measures, widen market network to improve
physical and financial performance of the  plant.

 Ministry and the company note the  recommendations of the Committee for implementation.   The Committee is
also informed that RINL management has been pursuing the goal of achieving high operational efficiencies,

enhancement of capacity utilization, cost control and expansion of market network.   The positive impact of these
measures is visible in the improved physical and financial performance of the company in the first half of the current
financial year.

AMR scheme OF RINL
 
The Committee opines that AMR scheme is essential for running the production units, as a continuous basis, at
their rated capacity.   The Committee is pleased to note that RINL is capable of making investment on AMR projects
through IEBR and nogovernment support is required for the purpose.   However, the Committee recommends that all
AMR schemes should be completed without time and cost overruns.
 
Action Taken
 
 Ministry and the Company note the recommendations of the Committee.
 
Recommendations ( Para 13.4  )
 
Proposal of long-term Comprehensive Turnaround Package
 
            The Committee is of the opinion that, since RINL has started to make cash profit and is poised to make net profit
by 2003-04, an opportunity should be given for turnaround.   The Committee observes that the proposal of long-term
Comprehensive Turnaround Package has long been under the consideration of Government.   The contention of the
Ministry of Finance, that, the expansion programme, at this stage, would only lead RINL to increased losses, is without
substance and logic, in view of the resurrection of the company (gearing up of the company to make profit) and
improving the steel scenario in general.   And when there no surplus manpower in RINL, there is no reason for adopting
VRS.   The Committee feels that the comprehensive turnaround plan should have got the nod of the Government for
ensuring the viability of the company.   RINL has got excellent lay out, effective and efficient management and devoted
workers.   The company may prove an anchor sheet of India Steel Industry.   The Comprehensive, Turnaround package
as prepared by M/s A.T. Kearney & MECON had the sound attributes for the revival of the company i.e. initiation of
action to create Holding company structure as an independent subsidiary to be styled as an infrastructure company; and
diversification of existing products-mix and enhancement of capacity to 4.0 million tonnes production with a investment
of Rs.1742 crore.   The revival plan also included raising of capital for funding the project and for repayment of debt
and interest.   That is why, the Committee, in its 30 th Report (On Demands for Grants 1999-2000), 37 th Report (on
Demands for Grants 1999-2000), 51 st Report (on Demands for Grants, 2001-02) and 70 th Report (on Demands for
Grants 2002-03) recommended the Government for giving the due consideration to the comprehensive turn around
proposal of RINL.  But, of no avail, track, and the only thing required is the one time assistance from the Government. 
Once the revival package is cleared by theGovernment, the plant would start running with appreciable acceleration, the
Committee hopes.

Short term turnaround proposal for revival of RINL.  
 
The Committee recommends that the Government should not hesitate in clearing the short term turnaround
proposal for revival of RINL.   The Committee is in agreement with the argument of RINL management that, setting of
accumulated losses of Rs.4981 crore (Provisional) as on 31 st March, 2002 against the preference share capital of
Rs.2937  crore and balance against equity capital, would not entail any cash outgo for the Government of India but
would definitely strengthen the balance sheet of the company.

As of now RINL is consistently improving both its physical and financial performance and no final decision has
been taken on the disinvestment proposal by the Department of Disinvestment.  The company is concentrating on  a
short term turn around strategy which consist of negotiations with LIC / UTI for partial conversions of loans into equity 
and reduction of interest rates.   The Govt. of India Guarantee for the working capital loans is being obtained for one
year at a time.   The above strategy is yielding desired results.

Reduction in cost of production.
 
The Committee further recommends that RINL management should explore the possibility of undertaking
measures for further reduction in cost of production.

Reducing the cost of production is a continuous process and a committee has also been set up headed by
Executive Director (Works) to look at areas of cost reduction.
 
 
 
 
 
Recommendations ( Para 17.4  )  
 
Price  determined by the free market forces of demand and supply
 
            The Committee opines that, in a liberal economy, price is determined by the free market forces of demand and
supply.  Strength of the competitors sets the motion of the market.   Therefore, in order to dominate the market one has
to be watchful and alert to have full and current knowledge of market forces.   The Committee is pleased to note that
RINL has the pricing cell in the marketing Department which collects the market related information like market price,
the quantum of demand and scale of supply of the products, competition prices, etc and the same is communicated to the
decision-makers.   The Committee recommends that adequate market research should be undertaken by the market wing
of RINL and, thereafter, system of market-related forecasting like demand trend, quantum of supply product-mix etc.
may be worked out in order to emerge a leader and manager of the market.   Quick decision making mechanism for
marketing purpose is a key to success.
 
Recommendations ( Para 17.8 ) 
 
 Consumer’s satisfaction.
 
The Committee is of the opinion that in a liberal and globalised economy customers is the king of market.  
Therefore, RINL management’s first and the foremost motto should be consumer’s satisfaction.  Meeting of customer’s
requirement in time should be the guiding principle of RINL’s management.   The marketing wing of RINL should
undertake measures for taking new market zones in India and abroad.

information of both traders and users.   The Management Information System collects and analyses the information on
demand trends, requirement of new products etc.
 
 
Recommendations ( Para  26.3  )

 Ultimate meta-goal of a corporate body
 
The Committee feels that industrial growth and development has real significance only when the benefits of
development reaches the lowest rungs of society, therefore, the ultimate meta-goal of a corporate body should be
directed towards this cherished direction.   True and total development means growth and development of each and all.  
IN this context the Committee appreciates the social obligation and responsibilities being shouldered by RINL by
undertaking projects on rehabilitation, basic infrastructure, education and health, alongwith special impetus to
upliftment of down trodden and empowerment of women.   The Committee hopes that RINL’s efforts for peripheral
development would continue and more funds would be provided for the purpose.

            RINL is continuously making efforts for the development and upliftment of the population of the surrounding
areas for enhancing peripheral development activities from the present level.  More budget was sought for the year
2003-04 for the growth and development of economically backward population.   Relevant training programmes have
also been taken up and a few developmental works like repair of roads, school buildings etc. are taken up on regular
basis.

Recommendations ( Para  2.3   )
 
 RINL operating as a separate and independent PSU (independent from SAIL)

independent PSU (independent from SAIL) for imbibing competitive resilience in plant, injecting operational efficiency

The Committee, however, recommends that the Government may like to examine and explore the possibility of
merger of SAIL and RINL and take concrete step in this regard, if the move consolidates long steel making capacity in

HARASSMENT OF DEFAULTING CEMENT UNITS
 
1.1       Recommendations  
 
Uttar Pradesh Finance Corporation portfolio has, at present, 48 cement  manufacturing units.  Out of 48 units only 2
units are regular in payment whereas 1 unit has recently gone in production.  As per the study conducted by the Uttar
Pradesh Finance Corporation, these units are facing problems relating to market recession like in transportation cost, wage
cost, ban on mining, unimplemented units, temporary default, etc.  The Committee notes the plethora of problems being
faced   by the cement units.  In the circumstances, the Committee observes that the reported harassment of these units,
instead of reviving them by the Uttar Pradesh Finance Corporation, as mentioned by the Association, needs to be looked
into.
(Para 5.10)
Action Taken
 
UPFC has submitted that there is no harassment of the defaulting cement units by the Corporation.  The Corporation
has been trying to contact every unit for One Time Settlement (OTS). The fact is that with the existing sale price of the
cement, none of the small scale units would be viable. The Corporation is of the view that though there has been
improvement in the demand of cement all over the country, the sales realization per bag has not improved. Even if such
units come into production they would not be able to break even and repay the Corporation’s dues. It would be in the
interest of the borrower to settle the dues of the Corporation through One Time Settlement only.
            Under the refinance scheme, SIDBI does not usually interfere with the decision on individual cases by PLIs
including SFCs.  Specific cases, if referred to, SIDBI may look into it in consultation with UPFC.
 
REVIVAL OF SICK SSI UNITS
1.2       Recommendation    
 
The Committee also notes that as per norms specified by the Reserve Bank of India, a sick unit is considered as
potentially viable, if it would be in a position, after implementing a relief package spread over a period not exceeding five
years from the commencement of the package from banks, financial institutions, Government (Central/State) and other
concerned agencies, as may be necessary, to continue to service its repayment obligations as agreed upon including those
forming part of the package, without the help of the concessions after the aforesaid period.  The repayment period of
restructuring debts should not exceed seven years from the date of implementation of the package.
(Para 6.5)
Action Taken
 
The Reserve Bank of India has issued revised, detailed, transparent and non-discretionary guidelines for
rehabilitation of current, sick and potentially viable Small Scale Industrial units, based on the recommendation of the Kohli
Committee, on 16th January, 2002.  Any proposal of revival, eligible under the above revised scheme, is examined by the
financing bank and necessary action taken, thereon.

THE DEMAND OF CEMENT  
 
2.1       Recommendation  
 
            The study report further mentioned that the immediate future is not very encouraging. However, once the
Government starts the revival of the economy through investment in infrastructure and construction activity picks up, the
demand for cement will grow.
(Para 5.3)
Action Taken
 
With the indications of revival of the economy in the recent months and growth in economic activity including
investments in housing and infrastructure sector, per capita consumption of cement is likely to go up driving such growth of
demand for cement with increasing GDP.
 
HARASSMENT OF DEFAULTING CEMENT UNITS
 
2.2       Recommendation    
 
            The Central Government had announced in the 8 th Five Year Plan about construction of double express highway,
houses for millions, generation of power to take the electricity to the rural areas.  Had such activities relating to
infrastructure building arisen the present state of low intake of Cement would not have arisen.  In fact, market demand of
cement was not in line with the Government’s projection.  In subsequent budgets of the Central Government the above
schemes did not find place, resulting in decline in demand of Cement.
(Para 5.11)
 
Action Taken 
 
There has been a growing thrust on infrastructure in  each subsequent budget and policy announcements. The Prime
Minister’s announcements in 1998 to construct 2 million houses annually during the 9 th Five Year Plan and to construct
concrete roads connecting the four mega cities covering around 6000 kms under the project- “ Golden Quadrilateral” and “
North-South, East-West Expressways” are significant. Implementation of such projects is likely to contribute to growth of
cement demand.

2.3
       Recommendation      
 
The giant units which take 5-6 years to produce cement started production in 1996 in UP after taking financial
assistance from IDBI on easy terms and flooded the market with cement at a cheaper rate and ousted smaller units by
waging an unfair and unequal competition. Had the development work regarding building up infrastructure started before
1992  or during 1992-96 the smaller units would have survived and established themselves.
(Para 5.12)
Action Taken
 
            IDBI had extended assistance to companies such as Mysore Cements Ltd., for setting up a 0.5 million tons per
annum grinding unit at Jhansi, U.P. (Rs. 7.3 crore @  17.5% p.a. in 1987 and further Rs. 3 crore @ 19.5% p.a. for

IDBI has not extended any soft loans to its assisted cement companies in UP. The assistance has been granted as per

EFFECT OF RISE IN COST OF POWER COUPLED WITH BORROWING COST ON THE
CEMENT INDUSTRY
 
3.1       Recommendation    
 
            Uttar Pradesh Financial Corporation made a study regarding mini cement plants financed by the Corporation. The
study report inter-alia  mentioned that the performance of the cement industry is closely linked with the industrial growth of
the country. In the period from 1993-94 to 1995-96, when the industrial growth was higher, the scenario in the segment was
bright. In 1995-96 with 11.7% industrial growth, the cement production grew at 10.6%. As the industry slowed down in
1996-97, so did the cement segment. The same downward trend continued in 1998-99. According to the industry sources,
the current take-off position is inadequate to generate more profits, as the low price realization is still not matching the
production cost. The recession in construction activity, low investment in major infrastructure projects, rise in the cost of
power etc. coupled with high borrowing cost has marked down the industry’s earnings.
(Para 5.1)
 
Action Taken
 
            The growth of cement industry was affected due to slowdown in the industrial growth and general economic
recession.
            Regarding cost of power, Ministry of Power is aware that for development of the economy, electricity has to be
affordable. To remain competitive in the global economy, Indian Industry needs to reduce the cost of inputs including
power. To address the issue of rising cost of power for industries etc., the Ministry of Power has adopted a two – pronged
strategy – Reduction of cost of power itself on the one hand and reduction and    elimination of cross subsidies, on the other.
The Ministry constituted an Inter-Disciplinary Group under the Chairmanship of Special Secretary (Power)  to go into the
question of reducing the cost of power.  The report of the Group is being implemented.  As regards reduction of cross
subsidies, the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998 empowers the Regulatory Commissions for the purpose. So far
13 State Electricity Regulatory Commissions have passed tariff orders, which reflect a trend towards tariff rationalization
and progressive reduction of cross subsidies.
            As regards high borrowing cost, the lending rates have gone down after the deregulation of interest rates regime. The
RBI in its mid-term review of monetary and credit policy for 2002-03 has cut the benchmark bank rate by quarter percent to
6.25 per cent and cash reserve ratio (CRR) to 4.75 per cent from 5 percent. The Commercial Banks are expected to lower
their lending rates for borrowers.  As per extant guidelines the banks are required to fix their own prime lending rates
(PLRs) and the maximum band over the PLR.  The interest rates on loans up to Rs. 2 lakh should not exceed the PLR and
that beyond Rs. 2 lakh is left to the discretion of the banks subject to PLR and the maximum bands.  The banks have been
advised to accord SSI units with a good track record the benefit of lower spreads over the PLR.
 
Further Recommendation
 
 
            The Ministry of Power has adopted a two pronged strategy – Reduction of cost of power  it self on the one hand and
reduction elimination of cross subsidies, on the other. The Committee would like to know how far reduction of the cost of
power,  tariff rationalization progressive reduction of  cross subsides  have been achieved in the state of Uttar Pradesh.
            The banks have been advised to accord SSI Units with a good track record, the benefit of lower spreads over the
PLR. The Committee would like to know how the number of SSI Units benefited by such advice given to the banks.

3.2
       Recommendation

doubled in the last four years. In 1996-97 the installed capacity was 96.25 million tonnes, going up to 105.25 million tonnes
in 1997-98. Some additional capacity is still expected to be installed in the coming years. Due to the huge capacity available
with major plants, they have encroached upon the segment of the mini cement plants by entering the remotest areas. Mini
cement plants,which traditionally used to cater to the local markets of remote areas, were therefore badly affected.
(Para 5.2)
Action Taken
 
            The Ministry of Commerce & Industry had requested Tariff Commission (erstwhile BICP) on January 22,1999 to
undertake a study of mini cement plants and suggest measures for their revival in view of deteriorating operational
efficiency. The Tariff Commission conducted the study on all India basis and submitted a report which, however, did not
recommend granting of any further concession to the mini cement plants.
            The report concluded that after delicensing of cement industry, as part of liberalization policy in 1991, the growth of
mini-cement plants stagnated. Large cement plants, on the other hand, registered higher growth both in capacity and
production. The large cement plants being high volume and low cost producers, contributing about 95 per cent of the total
cement production in the country, are the market price leaders. Mini cement plants are the followers and vulnerable to low
sales realization. From the recommendations of the Tariff Commission it emerges that revival of these units is possible only
when they improve their operational efficiency.  
 
Further Recommendation
 
            As a result of liberalization the cement industry has been delicensed. The result was stagnation of mini cement plants
and registration of higher growth by large cement plants. As per Tariff commission recommendation, these units can be
revived when they improve their operational efficiency. Tariff Commission has not given any plan of action in this regard.
Ministry of Small Scale Industries should suggest some measures to improve their operational efficiency.

Action Taken
 
The Banks / FIs usually determine the rate of interest to be charged on their term loans based on their cost of funds,
administrative overheads and also the risk perception of the borrower. Accordingly, the SFCs ( including UPFC) have been
retaining a margin of 3 % per annum over the rate of interest on refinance made available by IDBI and SIDBI.
With regard to the rate of interest charged by SIDBI on the refinance, it may be mentioned that the refinance rates,
as a matter of policy, are fixed below the prime lending rate (PLR) so that the cost of funds to the ultimate borrowers is
contained. With a view to mitigating the hardships of the SSI units because of the upward revision in interest rates during
early 1990s, SIDBI, in May,1995, gave an opportunity as a one time measure to SFCs including UPFC to review such cases
and claim refund of excess interest charged to certain categories of borrowers subject to the condition that similar benefit
should be passed on to their ultimate borrowers.
